findings.verdict_correction: The claim is correct except for one detail: parts-order-manager's create_internal_order is not the ONLY parts_orders creation path. Orders are also created by voice-to-parts-order (supabase/functions/voice-to-parts-order/index.ts:325), the iron_pull_part flow-engine action (supabase/functions/_shared/flow-engine/iron-actions.ts:273), and parts-order-manager's convert_parts_quote_to_order (supabase/functions/parts-order-manager/index.ts:1384, from the separate parts-department quoting flow). However, none of these paths reads quote_package_line_items, so accepted equipment quotes with part lines still never reach the parts module.
findings.title: Accepted equipment quotes with parts lines never reach the parts module — no order, no inventory movement, no fulfillment
findings.detail: Reps can add 'part' line items to quote_packages (line type allowed by m569, searched from parts_inventory/parts_catalog in searchQuotePackageItems), but the entire quote-builder-v2 edge function has zero references to parts_orders, parts_inventory, or parts_catalog — the string 'part' appears only in line-type validation lists (index.ts:213, 452). On quote acceptance the function advances the deal stage and writes qb_notifications, but never creates a parts_orders row, never decrements inventory, and never notifies the counter. The only parts_orders creation path is parts-order-manager's create_internal_order (index.ts:493). Consequence: parts sold through equipment quotes are invisible to parts fulfillment, and Account 360's lifetime-parts-spend rollup (built solely on parts_orders, m173:96-104) plus customer_parts_intelligence systematically undercount parts revenue.
findings.recommendation: On quote acceptance, have quote-builder-v2 materialize part-type line items into a draft parts_orders row (reusing parts-order-manager's line logic or a shared helper) with a FK back to the quote package, or publish a quote.accepted flow event with part lines that a flow workflow converts into a staged parts order for counter pick/fulfillment.

findings.verdict_correction: One minor phrasing imprecision: the parts_stock-backed stock_on_hand from the G4.1 lookup engine is what the parts-companion surface shows (via ai-parts-lookup → parts_lookup_engine); Iron's search does NOT use parts_stock — its lookup_part_inventory tool queries parts_catalog and parts_inventory and merges them (supabase/functions/_shared/iron/tools.ts:376-396), as the claim's own evidence list correctly states. So "companion/Iron search" should read "companion search (Iron separately merges the other two ledgers)". All other details are accurate.
findings.title: No shared parts availability source of truth: three unsynced stock ledgers (parts_catalog.on_hand, parts_inventory.qty_on_hand, parts_stock)
findings.detail: The DMS (CDK PARTMAST) import writes stock, backorder, and pricing exclusively to parts_catalog (on_hand, back_ordered, pricing_level_1..4). Service work-order fulfillment and counter-order picks decrement a separate legacy table, parts_inventory.qty_on_hand, via adjust_parts_inventory_delta_strict (m111/m121). A third Phase-3 ledger, parts_stock (m671, with qty_on_hand/qty_reserved/qty_allocated), backs the G4.1 lookup engine's stock_on_hand that the companion/Iron search shows — but is written only by transfer and cycle-count RPCs, never by imports or picks. No trigger, RPC, or function syncs any pair of these. The service-parts-planner makes pick/transfer/order decisions from parts_inventory (index.ts:216), which the DMS import never feeds, so the shop plans against stock numbers that diverge from the DMS on day one and drift further with every pick.
evidence: supabase/functions/_shared/parts-import-partmast.ts:214 (import reads/writes only parts_catalog incl. on_hand, back_ordered, pricing_level_1..4)
supabase/functions/_shared/iron/tools.ts:376-396 (Iron must query parts_catalog AND parts_inventory and merge)
findings.recommendation: Pick one canonical stock table (parts_catalog, since the DMS feeds it) and make adjust_parts_inventory_delta_strict operate on it, or add a migration that mirrors PARTMAST on_hand into parts_inventory per branch on every import and back-propagates pick deltas. Rewrite the m673 lookup stock CTE and the planner to read the same canonical source.

findings.verdict_correction: Two secondary details overstated. (a) _shared/service-invoice.ts:182 is the only AUTOMATIC producer of quickbooks_gl_sync_jobs, but supabase/functions/quickbooks-gl-sync/index.ts:102-112 also upserts a job row inside the admin-triggered sync_invoice action. findings.title: Counter/QRM-anchored rental revenue never reaches AR or QuickBooks
findings.detail: rental-billing-runner only mirrors a rental invoice into customer_invoices when contract.portal_customer_id is set ('AR mirror: requires a portal identity today... counter-only contracts note the skip'). Counter, Iron, and voice originated contracts anchor on qrm_company_id and get NO customer_invoices row, so their revenue is invisible to invoice aging, evaluate_credit_holds (which reads only customer_invoices), owner_data_miner_credit_exposure, and portal pay. Separately, even the portal-mirrored rows never sync to the GL: the only producer of quickbooks_gl_sync_jobs in the entire repo is _shared/service-invoice.ts:182 (service invoices); rental-billing-runner never enqueues a job and never sets quickbooks_gl_status, so no rental dollar ever reaches QuickBooks parity.
findings.recommendation: Make customer_invoices dual-anchored (portal_customer_id OR crm_company_id nullable with a CHECK that one exists), mirror every posted rental_invoices row regardless of origination channel, and enqueue a quickbooks_gl_sync_jobs row per mirrored invoice the same way _shared/service-invoice.ts does.

findings.verdict_correction: Claim is accurate as stated. Minor nuance: the Iron path (iron_initiate_rental_return) is itself gated behind the feature flag iron.flow.initiate_rental_return and creates the return at status 'inspection_pending', which further narrows real-world production of rental_returns rows beyond what the claim already states.
findings.title: Rental check-in creates no return record, inspection, or turnaround work order — damaged units are instantly re-rentable
findings.detail: The mig 773 inspection gate is check-OUT only. On check-in, rental-ops `code_line_return` (index.ts:809-851) just updates rental_contract_lines.status/return_meter_hours — it never creates a rental_returns row, an inspection_runs row, or a service_job. The mig 774 fleet-state trigger then flips the unit straight to availability='available'/readiness='available' (774:383-394). The 'Returned → condition inspection task' flow (rental-lifecycle-flows.ts:71-89) only inserts a crm_activities task telling staff to 'dispose damage in /ops/returns' — but the /ops/returns queue (RentalReturnsPage) is structurally empty because the only production producers of rental_returns are the Iron flow action iron_initiate_rental_return and the demo seed (scripts/demo/rental-seed.mjs). The entire damage-assessment/turnaround loop therefore never starts for counter-originated returns, which are the primary channel.
findings.recommendation: In rental-ops `code_line_return`, when a line (or the last line) is coded 'returned', auto-insert a rental_returns row stamped with rental_contract_id + equipment_id and open a rental_checkin inspection_runs row (mirror of the existing checkout template at index.ts:163). Gate the 774 fleet-state flip to 'available' on the return reaching a cleared disposition, so damaged or un-inspected iron cannot be re-rented.

findings.verdict_correction: One supporting detail is wrong in a way that strengthens the finding: the claim says "only tests and demo seeds populate" the *_cents columns, but the demo seed (scripts/demo/rental-seed.mjs:243) does not populate them either — its rental_returns upsert carries no charge fields. findings.title: Rental damage and return charges can never reach the final invoice — the billing planner reads cents columns nothing writes
findings.detail: The nightly rental-billing-runner folds return charges into the final invoice by reading rental_returns.fuel_charge_cents/cleaning_charge_cents/damage_charge_cents/environmental_fee_cents joined by rental_contract_id (index.ts:90-96), and rental-billing-core only includes damage when damage_disposition='customer_billable' (shared/rental-billing-core.ts:156-167). But NO production code writes those *_cents columns (mig 522:288-293 added them; only tests and demo seeds populate them) — the ops returns wizard writes the legacy dollars column charge_amount instead (RentalReturnsPage.tsx:522-529, 540-546). Compounding it, the only production producer of rental_returns (iron_initiate_rental_return, iron-actions.ts:898-908) inserts without rental_contract_id, so the billing runner's join can never even find the return. Assessed damage/fuel/cleaning charges silently bill $0 on every real contract.
findings.recommendation: Make the returns wizard (or rental-ops dispose_damage) persist the assessed amounts into the *_cents columns the planner reads, and stamp rental_contract_id in iron_initiate_rental_return. Add a check constraint or migration backfill mapping charge_amount → damage_charge_cents so existing rows bill correctly.

findings.verdict_correction: Directionally correct with two refinements. First, the dependency surface is larger than the seven cited modules: parts-network-optimizer/index.ts:481, OpportunityMapPage.tsx:95, PostSaleExperienceCenterPage.tsx:27, PortalPartsOrdersPage.tsx:89 (embedded join), and SQL RPCs/views in migrations 145 (trade exposure view), 147 (deal timing), 150 (health score), 157 (portal live status), and 262-270 (predictive plays) all read customer_fleet too. Second, 'these engines scan zero rows' is literally true for all of them, but parts-demand-forecast degrades gracefully rather than producing nothing — its fleet-hours signal is an optional uplift wrapped in try/catch (index.ts:280-305, comment 'customer_fleet may not exist in all deployments'), so forecasts still generate from sales history; the total no-op applies to parts-predictive-kitter, parts-predictive-failure, parts-predictive-ai, service-upsell-scanner's fleet recommendations, and portal-notification-refresh. findings.title: Sold equipment never becomes customer_fleet — the entire post-sale and predictive-parts stack reads a table no production workflow writes
findings.detail: customer_fleet (created in 082) re-declares machine identity (make, model, year, serial_number, current_hours) with a NULLABLE equipment_id FK to crm_equipment. Nothing in production creates rows: portal-api only SELECTs/UPDATEs it (routes /fleet, /fleet/:id/trade-interest), crm-router's closed-won path (resolveStage in _shared/crm-router-data.ts) has zero equipment or fleet side effects, and repo-wide grep finds no INSERT into customer_fleet in any edge function, migration, or frontend. Yet seven modules depend on it: parts-demand-forecast, parts-predictive-kitter, parts-predictive-failure, parts-predictive-ai, service-upsell-scanner, portal-notification-refresh, and the Asset 360 PartsTab (AssetDetailPage.tsx:237 resolves parts_orders only two-hop via customer_fleet.equipment_id → parts_orders.fleet_id). In production these engines scan zero rows and the machine's parts history is unreachable from its asset page.
findings.recommendation: On deal closed-won with a crm_deal_equipment role='subject' link, auto-create (or link) a customer_fleet row carrying equipment_id, purchase_deal_id, and warranty dates — a trigger on qrm_deals stage change or a crm-router side effect. Longer term, collapse customer_fleet identity fields into qrm_equipment (ownership='customer_owned') and keep customer_fleet as a thin join.

findings.verdict_correction: Claim is real with two detail fixes: (1) rental_invoices has existed since migration 522 (rental_intellidealer_financial_foundation), not 776; 776 is the L5 billing foundation that made rental billing live (invoice numbering, RPO accrual, nightly runner). (2) Rental is absent from the get_account_360 payload as a first-class key, but not 100% invisible on the page: rental-billing-runner mirrors posted rental invoices into customer_invoices (with crm_company_id) for portal-anchored contracts only, so an unpaid rental AR line can appear in Account 360's generic invoices list; QRM-company-only rental contracts produce no mirror, and no surface anywhere renders a customer's rental history or rental spend.
findings.title: No live total-customer-value view; rental is entirely absent from Account 360

findings.recommendation: Add a rental arm to get_account_360 (rental_contracts + rental_invoices matched on qrm_company_id OR via portal_customers.crm_company_id) and render lifetime/open rental spend on AccountCommandCenterPage next to parts and service, with the imported IntelliDealer facts shown as a reconciliation column rather than the only source.

findings.title: Parts customer spend is split-brain: Account 360 sees only portal orders, customer_parts_intelligence sees only counter orders
findings.detail: parts_orders has an either/or anchor (check constraint portal_customer_id OR crm_company_id, migration 132). The portal order insert sets only portal_customer_id even though portalCustomer.crm_company_id is loaded in the same request; the counter insert sets portal_customer_id: null + crm_company_id. Each consumer then reads only one side: get_account_360's parts lens joins strictly po.portal_customer_id → portal_customers (so all counter/phone/online orders are missing from the account's lifetime parts total), while parts-network-optimizer's customer_parts_intelligence filters .not('crm_company_id','is',null) (so all portal orders are missing from the intel card shown on QrmCompanyDetailPage/AccountCommandCenterPage). The same company gets two different parts-spend numbers, each wrong.
findings.recommendation: Stamp crm_company_id on portal-originated parts_orders at insert time (copy from portal_customers.crm_company_id), backfill existing rows, and change both get_account_360 and parts-network-optimizer to aggregate on the coalesced company anchor so one number exists.

findings.verdict_correction: Core claim stands with three detail refinements: (a) rental writes rental_invoices AND mirrors AR rows into customer_invoices (rental-billing-runner/index.ts:186, rental-ops/index.ts:278), so customer_invoices has rental writers too — this does not affect the equipment/parts gap; (b) demo-seed migrations 389/390 do insert parts-order-linked customer_invoices rows (and migration 477 backfills invoice_type='parts' on them), but these are one-time synthetic seed data for workspace 'default', not an order-to-cash workflow — no production code path invoices a delivered parts order; (c) parts_invoice_lines is also referenced by docs files and by an UPDATE-only SQL function (adjust_parts_invoice_ldttn, migration 533), but database.types.ts remains the only non-migration code reference and there are zero INSERT paths, so 'zero writers' holds in the sense that nothing can ever populate the table.
findings.title: Equipment-sale and parts revenue never reach invoicing — order-to-cash exists for only 2 of 4 streams
findings.detail: Service creates customer_invoices (generateInvoiceForServiceJob, service_post_internal_billing_to_invoice) and rental creates rental_invoices, but the two largest streams dead-end before AR: quote-builder-v2/index.ts contains zero references to customer_invoices (an accepted equipment quote never becomes an invoice), and parts-order-manager/index.ts contains zero invoice references (a delivered parts order never becomes an invoice). No code anywhere — edge functions, web app, or scripts — inserts a customer_invoices row with invoice_type='equipment', yet an entire equipment-reversal foundation (reverse_equipment_sale_with_approval, record_equipment_reversal_manager_approval, reversal candidate views filtered on invoice_type='equipment') guards invoices that no workflow can create. The parts_invoice_lines detail table (migration 468, whose header comment claims customer_invoices is 'already used by parts orders') has zero writers in the entire repo.
evidence: supabase/migrations/468_parts_invoice_lines_customer_invoices.sql:24 (table created; only repo-wide reference outside migrations is apps/web/src/lib/database.types.ts)
findings.recommendation: Add invoice generation at the natural lifecycle points: quote-builder-v2 accept action writes a customer_invoices row with invoice_type='equipment' (unblocking the existing reversal foundation), and parts-order-manager's delivered transition writes customer_invoices + parts_invoice_lines with invoice_type='parts'. Both should call next_invoice_number and enqueue quickbooks_gl_sync_jobs like the service path does.

findings.verdict_correction: Two immaterial detail refinements: the parts 25% floor at migration 676 line ~382 is the seeded rule definition; the actual clamping enforcement is in parts_resolve_priced_line at lines 539 and 609-619. Also, rental-ops writes the unchecked rate in two places on create (line 406 for the contract estimate and line 445 for the contract line's daily_rate_cents). rental_rate_rules does have an approved_by column (mig 771), but it is rate-card authorship metadata, not a per-contract discount gate — the core claim stands.
findings.title: Rental is the only revenue stream with no margin/discount gate — counter can set any rate
findings.detail: The other three streams enforce floors server-side: equipment quotes route below-threshold margins through qb_margin_thresholds + quote_approval_cases in quote-builder-v2; parts have a hard 25% margin floor and 5% counter discount cap enforced in parts_resolve_priced_line (margin_floor_applied); service-quote-engine computes floor_margin_pct per rate rule and sets floor_blocked, blocking quotes below floor. Rental has nothing: rental-ops accepts body.daily_rate with only a '> 0' check (toCurrencyAmount at line 366, stored at 406), agreed_* rates default from estimates with no comparison to the resolved book rate from rental_resolve_rates, and migration 771's rate engine has no cost basis, floor, or discount concept. The only rental 'rate mismatch' exception is the portal-vs-qrm id-space check, not a pricing guard. L7 yield suggestions only write INACTIVE draft rules.
evidence: supabase/migrations/771_l1_rental_rate_engine.sql (no margin/floor logic; only 'floored at zero' proration comment at line 21)
findings.recommendation: Enforce a rental rate floor in rental-ops (and the contract-open DB trigger): compare agreed/estimate rates to the rental_resolve_rates book rate and either block or require manager approval (enqueue_exception 'rental_rate_below_floor' mirroring the quote approval-case pattern) when the discount exceeds a workspace-configured threshold in qb_margin_thresholds or finance_foundation_config.

findings.verdict_correction: Directionally correct with two small imprecisions: the rental-billing-runner customer_invoices AR-mirror insert is at supabase/functions/rental-billing-runner/index.ts:186 (not 182), and the account map does not fail to classify rental/equipment lines — inferRevenueAccount silently misclassifies them into misc_revenue_account_id via its fallback, so a manually synced rental invoice would post to the wrong GL account rather than error. Likewise quickbooks-gl-sync's loadInvoice (index.ts:39-56) is generic over customer_invoices (it selects service_job_id but does not require it), so manual sync of a rental invoice technically works — it just posts to misc revenue.
findings.title: QuickBooks GL sync is reachable only from service invoices; rental never enqueues and the account map cannot classify rental or equipment revenue
findings.detail: The only writer of quickbooks_gl_sync_jobs in the repo is _shared/service-invoice.ts:182 (plus manual per-invoice sync from the admin page). rental-billing-runner's AR mirror insert and rental-ops' deposit/extension invoices never enqueue a sync job, so even portal-anchored rental revenue reaches QuickBooks only if an admin manually syncs each invoice. Worse, the QuickBooks credential/account mapping (quickbooks-gl.ts) defines service_revenue_account_id, parts_revenue_account_id, haul_revenue_account_id, shop_supplies_account_id, misc_revenue_account_id, and tax_liability_account_id — there is no rental or equipment revenue account, so those streams cannot post to the correct GL account even if invoices existed and were enqueued.
findings.recommendation: Add rental_revenue_account_id and equipment_revenue_account_id to the QuickBooks credential schema and line classification, and enqueue quickbooks_gl_sync_jobs from rental-billing-runner, rental-ops invoice creation, and the new equipment/parts invoice paths so all four streams share one GL pipeline.

findings.verdict_correction: The unbounded-query + client-side-join pattern is exactly as claimed, but because supabase/config.toml:8 sets PostgREST max_rows = 1000, each of the four unbounded selects is silently truncated at 1000 rows rather than transferring the whole parts domain. At real dealer scale (tens of thousands of SKUs x per-branch inventory rows) the dominant failure mode is silent data corruption — arbitrary parts missing from the catalog list, understated stock totals/byBranch cells, and broken reorder/forecast joins (inventory rows joined against a truncated 1000-row slice of profiles/forecasts) — plus wasted transfer of up to ~4,000 rows on every mount (staleTime 30s). Still a critical unbounded list-view scan per CLAUDE.md; the 'transfers the entire domain' framing only becomes literally true if max_rows is raised.
findings.title: Parts catalog page pulls four entire tables to the browser and joins them in JS
findings.detail: usePartsCatalog() runs parts_catalog .select('*') with no .limit()/.range() (only ordered by part_number). PartsCatalogPage additionally fetches ALL parts_inventory rows ('part_number, qty_on_hand, branch_id, bin_location', unbounded), ALL parts_reorder_profiles rows (unbounded), and a month of parts_demand_forecasts, then builds totals/byBranch/reorder/forecast Maps client-side. A real dealer parts catalog is tens of thousands of SKUs x per-branch inventory rows, so this page transfers the whole parts domain on every mount (staleTime only 30s), exactly the unbounded list-view scan CLAUDE.md forbids.
findings.recommendation: Replace with a server-side paginated/searchable view or RPC that returns catalog rows joined with per-branch qty, reorder point, and forecast risk (one query, .range() paginated), and select explicit columns instead of '*'. Keep client state to the visible page only.

findings.verdict_correction: The claim that amount_paid 'is only ever written by the Stripe portal path' is slightly incomplete: portal_record_invoice_payment (migration 113, exposed via portal-api's POST invoices/pay subroute) is a second, non-Stripe writer. However it is a customer-portal self-report endpoint hard-gated to get_portal_customer_id(), so the core claim stands: there is no staff-side receive-payment/cash-application workflow for checks, wires, ACH, or counter tender, and no AR payment ledger table at all.
findings.title: No AR cash receipts or payment application — checks/ACH/cash cannot be recorded against invoices
findings.detail: customer_invoices.amount_paid is only ever written by the Stripe portal path (portal-stripe + _shared/portal-stripe-reconcile.ts). There is no receive-payment workflow for the payment types equipment dealers actually collect (checks, wires, ACH, counter cash/card): no customer_payments table, no record-AR-payment RPC, no cash-application UI, and no card-present option. The AP side got exactly this in migration 661 (record_ap_payment with double-pay guard), but the AR side of the K1.1 'native AR system of record' has nothing. Downstream, AR dunning (664), credit holds (evaluate_credit_holds), and owner credit-exposure views all compute off amount_paid, so any non-Stripe payment leaves customers falsely delinquent. The parts counter POS only stamps a payment_received_at timestamp with no tender type or amount (parts-order-manager/index.ts:447).
findings.recommendation: Build a receive-payments desk: a customer_payments table + record_ar_payment RPC (mirroring the 661 AP guard pattern) with tender type, reference number, and multi-invoice application; wire it into finance-enforcement UI, counter POS, and rental Command Center; add Stripe Terminal for card-present. Have it update amount_paid/status so dunning and credit holds become truthful.

findings.title: Equipment sale invoicing does not exist — the largest revenue line has a reversal path but no forward billing path
findings.detail: Nothing in the codebase creates a customer_invoices row with invoice_type='equipment'. Migration 471 defines the equipment_invoices view over rows 'deliberately marked equipment' and explicitly declines to backfill, quote-builder-v2/index.ts (8,764 lines) contains zero customer_invoices writes on accept/sign, and crm-router's mark-sold path bills nothing. Yet the reversal machinery (find_equipment_invoice_reversal_candidate, reverse_equipment_sale_by_stock_number in migrations 540/659/667, wired into _shared/crm-router-data.ts:2510) presumes those invoices exist. Service bills (service-billing-post), rental bills (rental-billing-runner), but a won equipment deal — with trade credit, deposit application, FET, and county tax — never becomes an invoice, so equipment revenue never reaches AR, dunning, Form 8300, or margin reporting.
findings.recommendation: Add a deal-settlement workflow: on the salesOrderSigned→delivered transition, generate a customer_invoices row (invoice_type='equipment') from the accepted quote_package — applying deposits, trade credit, tax-calculator output, and FET — using the branch-prefixed numbering from migration 662. Emit a deal.invoiced flow event so AR, dunning, and exec margin surfaces see equipment revenue.

findings.verdict_correction: One qualifier: the quote builder is not entirely governance-free. It enforces a deal-level margin floor with manager approval + justification (apps/web/src/features/quote-builder/lib/quote-workspace.ts:290-291, components/MarginFloorGate.tsx) and an owner approval case gating customer-facing sends (lib/quote-builder-approval-blocker.ts). However, this is aggregate whole-quote margin governance — it never consults the parts pricing ruleset, per-line parts floors, customer/volume price overrides, or the 5% cap, and it records no per-line parts discount_authority trail. So 'no discount approval' should read 'no parts-ruleset-aware, per-line discount authority; only an aggregate deal-margin gate'. The core claim stands.
findings.title: Quote builder prices parts with raw list price, bypassing the server-side parts pricing engine and discount governance
findings.detail: Migration 676 built an enforceable parts pricing resolver — parts_customer_prices, parts_volume_prices, parts_resolve_priced_line() with min-margin checks and the 5% counter discount cap, plus discount authority/approval columns on parts_order_lines and parts_quote_lines. Its only consumer is parts-order-manager (rpc call at index.ts:297). The sales quote builder instead reads parts_catalog.list_price/cost_price directly (quote-api.ts:2915, 3000-3010) with no customer-specific price, no volume tier, no margin floor from the parts ruleset, and no discount approval. The same customer can be quoted a different parts price by a sales rep than the counter is allowed to charge, and quote-side parts discounts have no authority trail.
findings.recommendation: Route part-line pricing in searchQuotePackageItems / quote save through the parts_resolve_priced_line RPC, passing the deal's qrm_company_id, so customer-specific and volume pricing plus min-margin/discount-cap enforcement apply identically at the counter and inside equipment quotes.

findings.verdict_correction: One detail is imprecise: deal lifecycle flow events ARE published — migration 194_flow_engine_foundation.sql:396 attaches trg_flow_emit_deal on qrm_deals, emitting 'deal.created' and 'deal.stage.changed' (payload includes closed_at) into the flow bus. They come from a DB trigger, not crm-router (crm-router indeed publishes nothing). However, no flow workflow or subscriber routes those events to post-sale-parts-playbook, and no 'deal.closed_won' event is ever emitted, so the core claim stands: the playbook loop never fires automatically and is never surfaced in the deal-owning rep's sales/QRM surfaces.
findings.title: Deal-won parts follow-on loop never fires automatically and is invisible to the rep who is supposed to send it
findings.detail: Migration 280's design is explicit: 'When a QRM deal closes_won on equipment, Claude auto-generates a 30/60/90-day parts plan... The rep reviews, tweaks, then sends.' The post-sale-parts-playbook function supports a batch cron path over the eligible_deals_for_playbook RPC (whose comment says 'Cron reads this'), but no migration schedules it — grep of supabase/migrations for post-sale-parts-playbook returns nothing — and crm-router has no closed_won hook and publishes no deal lifecycle flow events. The only trigger surface is parts-companion's PostSalePlaysPage (via post-sale-api.ts:116), a parts-staff page. QrmDealDetailPage.tsx contains zero parts references and features/sales has zero references to playbooks or parts intelligence, so the rep who owns the closed deal never sees the playbook.
findings.recommendation: Add a pg_cron schedule invoking the batch path of post-sale-parts-playbook, and surface generated playbooks on QrmDealDetailPage and the sales Today feed with a review-and-send action, closing the loop m280 designed (draft -> reviewed -> sent -> accepted vs. actual parts orders).

findings.title: Trade-in keep_recondition flow (migration 766) never opens or reconciles a reconditioning service work order
findings.detail: Migration 766 builds the trade-recondition margin gate (qb_trade_ins.reconditioning_approval_status, trade_valuations.expected_gross_margin_pct, trade_recondition_approval_audit, material-change re-approval config) entirely on the rep-entered reconditioning_estimate. It contains zero references to service_jobs — every 'service' match in the file is a service_role grant. The service engine already supports work_class 'reconditioning' posting to 'used_unit_landed_cost' (migration 691), but the only code paths that create internal service jobs are rental damage disposition (rental-ops) and the flow-engine open_internal_service_job action used by rental flows. No workflow opens a reconditioning WO when a trade is approved with disposition 'keep_recondition', service_internal_cost_postings carries machine_id but no trade_in/valuation FK, and the H10 posting RPC never writes actual costs back to qb_trade_ins/trade_valuations — so the material-change re-approval threshold (10%/$2,500 in finance_foundation_config) can never fire from real shop actuals. Additionally, record_trade_recondition_manager_approval (766:1050) has no caller in any edge function or frontend file, so the approval gate itself is inoperable from the product.
findings.recommendation: When qb_trade_ins.disposition='keep_recondition' reaches reconditioning_approval_status='approved' (or the deal closes), auto-create a service_jobs row with request_type='internal', service_internal_work_class='reconditioning', machine_id linked to the intaken trade unit, and a trade_in_id/trade_valuation_id column on service_jobs or service_internal_cost_postings. On internal cost posting, compare total_cost_cents against trade_valuations.reconditioning_estimate and re-run qep_trade_recondition_material_change to flip status to 'stale' when actuals breach the threshold. Wire record_trade_recondition_manager_approval into an approvals UI (e.g., sales My Approvals).

findings.verdict_correction: Core claim holds, but one mechanism detail is wrong: deal lifecycle events ARE published — not by crm-router, but by DB trigger trg_flow_emit_deal on qrm_deals (supabase/migrations/194_flow_engine_foundation.sql:354-397), which emits 'deal.created' and 'deal.stage.changed' into analytics_events via emit_event(); flow-runner polls these, and flow-synthesize's EVENT_TAXONOMY (supabase/functions/flow-synthesize/index.ts:43) permits synthesizing a workflow on deal.stage.changed with open_internal_service_job in its ACTION_CATALOG. So the plumbing to react to stage changes exists. What actually keeps stage 17 honor-system: (a) none of the ~30 shipped workflow files in supabase/functions/_shared/flow-workflows/ triggers on any deal.* event (all trigger_event_patterns verified — rental.*, quote.*, parts.*, iron.intent.*, voice.*, etc.); (b) the deal.stage.changed payload (194:377-387) carries deal_id/stage_id but no equipment_id, and open_internal_service_job skips without params.equipment_id (registry.ts:415), so even a synthesized workflow could not open a machine-specific make-ready WO from that event alone; (c) no code path anywhere writes service_internal_work_class='pdi_new_prep' (only writers: rental-ops/index.ts:918 and registry.ts:423, both defaulting to 'rental_fleet_maintenance'). Minor nit: pdi_new_prep grep also hits 691's test file (691_h10_internal_rental_fleet_service.test.ts:23), not solely the migration.
findings.title: A sold machine never triggers a PDI/make-ready work order — stage 17 'Equipment Ready' is a manual honor-system gate
findings.detail: The owner's 21-step pipeline stage 17 'Equipment Ready' requires 'Machine washed, attachments installed, PDI complete, payment confirmed' (066:68), but nothing in code enforces or automates it: the only other reference to that stage is a label mapping in migration 331. The service engine's 'pdi_new_prep' internal work class (with new_unit_prep cost destination) has zero writers anywhere in the repo — grep hits only migration 691 itself. The PDI checklist that does exist lives on equipment_intake.pdi_checklist (a jsonb array updated directly by PdiChecklistPage), and equipment_intake has an equipment_id FK but no deal linkage (only a free-text demand_assessment 'retail_deal' flag), no technician assignment, and no labor/parts tracking through service_jobs. crm-router publishes no deal lifecycle events (no flow-bus publish calls), so no flow workflow can react to Deposit Collected/closed-won to open a make-ready WO.
findings.recommendation: Emit deal.stage.changed / deal.deposit_collected from the crm-router write path onto the flow bus, and add a flow workflow that opens a service_jobs row (request_type='internal', work_class='pdi_new_prep', machine_id from crm_deal_equipment subject unit) when a deal hits Deposit Collected. Block or badge the 'Equipment Ready' stage transition until that WO closes, replacing the disconnected equipment_intake jsonb checklist for retail deals.

findings.verdict_correction: The core claim holds — no deal, signal, move, or crm_activity is ever created from a service touchpoint — but "read-only and unpersisted" is slightly overstated on two edges: (1) the ServiceToSalesPage trade-up draft IS persisted to email_drafts (supabase/functions/draft-email/index.ts:172) with company_id, equipment_id, and context.source_surface='service_to_sales', and it surfaces in a rep-facing review/edit/send/dismiss queue (apps/web/src/features/email-drafts/lib/email-drafts-api.ts) with pending/edited/sent/dismissed status tracking — so there is minimal act-tracking at the draft level, just no pipeline entry (sending a draft never logs a crm_activity; /send and /mark-sent only update email_drafts status). (2) Completion feedback does persist service-side knowledge (machine_knowledge_notes, job_code_observations, service_job_events) — it is specifically the upsell_suggestions column that is write-only. Additionally, a service-to-sales automation exists but is dead wiring: _shared/flow-workflows/service-delay-strategic-account.ts would create a crm_activities follow-up task via the create_task flow action (supabase/functions/_shared/flow-engine/registry.ts:46-68) on 'service.job.delayed', but no code anywhere emits any service.* flow event, so it can never fire.
findings.title: Service touchpoints generate zero sales leads — the entire service-to-sales loop is read-only and unpersisted
findings.detail: Every service-to-sales bridge dead-ends before creating a deal, signal, move, or activity. (1) service-upsell-scanner computes PM/recall/repeat-failure recommendations on the fly and returns them only in the HTTP response (index.ts:119) to the technician-facing ServiceJobDetailDrawer 'PM / upsell scan' button — nothing is persisted and nothing reaches a sales surface. (2) Technician upsell_suggestions captured at job completion are written to service_completion_feedback (service-completion-feedback/index.ts:86) but no code anywhere reads that column — OperatorIntelligencePage and ReputationSurfacePage select other columns. (3) The QRM ServiceToSalesPage builds a 'replacement motion queue' client-side from service_jobs + crm_equipment + fleet_intelligence, but its only mutation is a draft email into email_drafts — no deal, no crm_activity, no signal, no move is ever created, so the 'high repair cost → replacement opportunity' motion has no pipeline entry point and no tracking of whether anyone acted.
findings.recommendation: Persist upsell-scanner output and completion-feedback upsell_suggestions into the existing signals/deal_signals bridge (migration 207 pattern) keyed by company_id, and give ServiceToSalesPage a 'Create opportunity' action that opens a qrm_deals row via crm-router with the machine linked through crm_deal_equipment (role trade_in/subject), so service-driven replacement cases enter the pipeline and are measurable.

findings.verdict_correction: Two details are wrong but strengthen rather than weaken the claim: (1) migration 767_purge_demo_seed_data.sql never touches fleet_intelligence — it purges QRM/CRM demo tables only; in fact no fleet_intelligence demo seed ever existed anywhere in repo history, so the table has been writer-less since its creation in migration 013, not merely since a purge. (2) ReplacementPredictionPage.tsx does not display outreach_status — it never selects that column (it selects outreach_deal_value); outreach_status is read by ServiceToSalesPage.tsx:141 and relationship-engine.ts:228, and is never writable from any surface.
findings.title: fleet_intelligence replacement predictions have no production writer, starving every service-to-sales replacement surface
findings.detail: The 'aging fleet / predicted replacement' half of the service-to-sales motion runs entirely on the fleet_intelligence table (predicted_replacement_date, replacement_confidence, outreach_status, outreach_deal_value). Repo-wide, that table has only readers: ServiceToSalesPage, ReplacementPredictionPage, qrm-command-center's relationship engine, chat, and customer-profile. No edge function, trigger, migration backfill, or script inserts/updates rows (demo seeds were purged in migration 767). ReplacementPredictionPage is also purely read-only — outreach_status is displayed but never writable. So the replacement-opportunity lens across QRM renders empty in production and no service/telematics data (engine hours, repair frequency, service spend from service_jobs) ever feeds a replacement prediction.
findings.recommendation: Add a cron scan (mirroring deal-timing-scan) that computes fleet_intelligence rows from real signals already in the schema — service_jobs frequency/spend per machine_id, qrm_equipment.engine_hours vs equipment_lifecycle_summary, telematics_feeds utilization — and make outreach_status writable from ReplacementPredictionPage/ServiceToSalesPage so worked leads leave the queue.

findings.verdict_correction: Two detail refinements: (a) parts_orders (migration 082) is a customer self-service parts ordering table, not a vendor procurement table, so it would be the wrong destination for vendor demand anyway — the true gap is that NO parts-procurement PO table exists (vendor_purchase_orders is explicitly commented as being for 'non-parts buys'). (b) The planner does not write a free-text po_reference at all — it leaves po_reference NULL; the only writer is service-vendor-inbound backfilling it from parsed vendor replies, which strengthens the claim: absent a vendor email, every vendor-order action hits the 72h missing-PO escalation by design. Also, the parts department does get non-PO visibility of shop activity (parts-reorder-compute reads consumed service_parts_requirements for reorder math; planner events mirror to fulfillment runs shown on PartsFulfillmentPage), but nothing creates an actionable purchase order record.
findings.title: Service parts 'order' plan actions dead-end: they never create a vendor_purchase_orders or parts_orders record
findings.detail: When service-parts-planner decides a requirement must be vendor-ordered, it only inserts a service_parts_actions row (action_type='order', free-text po_reference from m095:51) and flips the requirement to 'ordering'. No code path creates a row in vendor_purchase_orders (m347) or parts_orders: grep shows vendor_purchase_orders appears in zero edge functions and is only touched by the parts feature's PurchaseOrdersPage/PurchaseOrderDetailPage UI. vendor_purchase_order_lines has FKs to qb_equipment_models/qrm_companies but no service_parts_requirement_id or service_job_id. The parts department therefore never sees the shop's vendor demand in its PO workflow and must re-key orders manually; the vendor escalator then chases 'missing PO' actions that the system itself never let anyone create (service-vendor-escalator seeds escalations for order actions with blank po_reference after 72h).
findings.recommendation: Have service-parts-planner (or a service-parts-manager action) create a draft vendor_purchase_orders row grouped by vendor, add service_parts_requirement_id to vendor_purchase_order_lines, and write the resulting PO number back into service_parts_actions.po_reference so the escalator and the parts PO pages track the same object.

findings.verdict_correction: Two detail fixes: (a) parts_orders is created in migration 082_customer_portal.sql:127, not 132 — migration 132_parts_module_schema.sql:74-96 only extends it with crm_company_id/order_source/etc. (still no service_job_id anywhere). (b) 'linked_service_job_id could never be populated even if events were emitted' is slightly overstated: migration 115_parts_fulfillment_and_profile_workspaces.sql gives both parts_orders.fulfillment_run_id and service_jobs.fulfillment_run_id FKs to the shared parts_fulfillment_runs table, so an indirect join path exists that a future emitter could use to resolve the linked job. There is no direct column and no emitter exists, so the workflow can indeed never fire today.
findings.title: Parts backorder blocks a job stage but never reschedules it, and the parts-received flow workflow can never fire (no event producer, no job link on parts_orders)
findings.detail: The stage machine does block: approved→parts_pending→parts_staged→scheduled (service-job-router:68-70), service-stage-enforcer auto-advances only when every requirement is staged/consumed, and service-tat-monitor flags parts_pending SLA breaches. But the feedback loop is one-way and dated at plan time: need_by_date is derived once from service_jobs.scheduled_start_at (planner:247-250); when service-vendor-inbound later updates an order action's expected_date past the scheduled start, nothing touches scheduled_start_at, notifies the scheduler, or re-plans. The flagship flow workflow parts-received-for-open-job triggers on 'parts.item.received' with a condition on event.properties.linked_service_job_id, but no producer exists anywhere (the only other reference is a string list in flow-synthesize/index.ts:47), and parts_orders (m132) has no service_job_id column, so the linked_service_job_id property could never be populated even if events were emitted.
evidence: supabase/functions/_shared/flow-workflows/parts-received-for-open-job.ts:4-6 ('will be wired in Slice 3+' — never was)
findings.recommendation: Add emit_event() triggers on service_parts_actions/requirement status changes and on parts receiving (mirroring rental's m775 pattern), add a nullable service_job_id to parts_orders, and add a flow workflow or enforcer pass that flags jobs whose max(expected_date) exceeds scheduled_start_at and proposes a reschedule to the advisor.

findings.title: Service quotes price parts at manually-entered unit_cost ?? 0 — CDK list price and pricing levels in parts_catalog are never consulted
findings.detail: service-quote-engine builds customer-facing part lines with unit_price = requirement.unit_cost ?? 0 (index.ts:582-596). service_parts_requirements.unit_cost is caller-supplied (service-parts-manager index.ts:195,230) or copied from job_codes.parts_template (_shared/service-parts-from-job-code.ts:38); nothing ever looks up parts_catalog.list_price or pricing_level_1..4 that the PARTMAST import maintains, nor parts_vendor_prices. So the shop quotes parts at internal cost — or $0 when the advisor leaves it blank — while the parts module holds the real retail matrix. There is no markup logic anywhere in the service quote path (grep for list_price/pricing_level in service-quote-engine and service-parts-manager returns nothing).
findings.recommendation: When a requirement is added (or at quote generation), resolve part_number against parts_catalog and populate both cost and a sell price from list_price/pricing levels with a workspace markup matrix; flag lines that fall back to $0 as quote blockers instead of silently quoting free parts.

findings.verdict_correction: Reservations for service parts are effectively schema-only, but qty_reserved is not entirely writer-less: parts_reserve_interbranch_transfer (supabase/migrations/674_g51_multi_location_stock_transfers.sql:361, called from supabase/functions/parts-order-manager/index.ts:1213) increments parts_stock.qty_reserved for inter-branch transfer reservations. However, it never fires for service_parts_requirements, has no frontend caller, and writes to the Phase-3 parts_stock table while all pick paths (service_parts_apply_fulfillment_action and parts-order-manager counter picks) decrement the legacy parts_inventory.qty_on_hand via adjust_parts_inventory_delta_strict — so pending service requirements still hold no stock, and the pick-time INSUFFICIENT_STOCK race between service jobs and counter orders is real.
findings.title: Reservations are schema-only: pending service requirements hold no stock and parts_stock.qty_reserved is never written
findings.detail: The Phase-3 schema created qty_reserved/qty_allocated on parts_stock (m671:330-339), but grep across all migrations, edge functions, and the web app finds zero writers of qty_reserved. Adding a service_parts_requirement reserves nothing; inventory only moves at pick time via adjust_parts_inventory_delta_strict. The planner de-conflicts stock only in-memory within a single plan batch (takeStock in service-parts-planner:360,395) — two jobs planned hours apart can both be told to 'pick' the same last unit, and the second tech discovers INSUFFICIENT_STOCK at the shelf. Counter orders (parts-order-manager pick, index.ts:1092-1100) race against service picks on the same parts_inventory rows with no allocation priority.
evidence: supabase/migrations/121_service_parts_fulfillment_transaction_rpc.sql:48-53 (stock conflict surfaces only as INSUFFICIENT_STOCK at pick time)
supabase/functions/parts-order-manager/index.ts:1092-1100 (counter picks hit the same rows unreserved)
findings.recommendation: Introduce a reservation step: when the planner marks a line 'picking', increment a reserved quantity (on the canonical stock table) and have adjust_parts_inventory_delta_strict check on_hand - reserved for counter sales; release reservations on cancel/return.

findings.title: RPO rent-to-purchase conversion dead-ends in a follow-up task — no deal ever carries the accrued credit
findings.detail: L5 accrues rpo_credit_accrued_cents on paid RPO invoices and emits rental.rpo.threshold_reached (mig 776), but the only consumer, the rental-rpo-threshold workflow, executes a single create_task action producing a generic follow_up activity. No code path anywhere creates a qrm_deals row from a rental contract, transfers the accrued credit into a deal amount, or links the contract to the sales pipeline — even though the roadmap ticket L5.1 (mig 768) explicitly specifies 'RPO conversion creates a qrm_deals row carrying accrued credit'. The accrued balance is visible only inside the rental_resolve_context JSON (Iron chat); no operator UI reads rpo_credit_accrued_cents (grep: only database.types.ts and the task template string).
findings.recommendation: Add a convert_rpo action (crm-router or rental-ops) that creates a qrm_deals row FK-linked to the rental contract, seeds amount = rpo_purchase_price_cents − rpo_credit_accrued_cents, and links the unit via crm_deal_equipment; have the rental-rpo-threshold workflow create that draft deal instead of (or alongside) the task.

findings.verdict_correction: Two minor detail fixes: (a) the native_signature_id check-out requirement is at supabase/migrations/770_l0_rental_checkout_security_gate.sql:94-95, not 47-48 (lines 47-48 are the draft→quoted→reserved lifecycle transitions); (b) rental-ops sets line status 'quoted' (index.ts:448) but no current code writes contract-level lifecycle_state='quoted' — that transition is merely permitted by the 770 guard, and the 'quoted' contract status otherwise appears only in the portal request lifecycle (submitted→reviewing→quoted) read paths.
findings.title: No rental quoting path through the quote builder — rental quotes have no document, e-signature, or margin approval
findings.detail: A rental 'quote' is just lifecycle_state='quoted' on rental_contracts with line status 'quoted' set by rental-ops; it never touches quote_packages. The 8,764-line quote-builder-v2 engine's only rental reference is the 'rental_conversion' availability candidate type. Consequently rental quotes get none of the sales-quote machinery: no customer-facing document/deal-room share token, no e-sign (rental check-out instead requires native_signature_id via a separate path), no quote_approval_cases margin gate, and no qb_quote_outcomes win/loss analytics — despite the mission being equipment sales AND rental.
findings.recommendation: Either add a rental package type to quote_packages (lines referencing rental_contract_lines, rate-rule resolution via the L1 engine, share/e-sign via the existing deal-room token path) or build a minimal rental quote document + approval case that reuses quote_signatures and the margin-floor gate, so 'quoted' contracts produce something a customer can see and sign.

findings.verdict_correction: Two minor detail fixes, neither changing the verdict: (1) ar_credit_blocks has more readers than claimed — beyond apply_ar_override and HealthScoreDrawer.tsx:149, it is read by account-360 RPCs (migs 173/355/366/397), L-stream gates 773:86 and 777:54, and the QRM ARCreditBlockBanner.tsx override UI — but none of them inserts rows, so 'no automated producer' holds (in fact no code path creates rows at all). (2) evaluate_credit_holds is not cron-automated; it runs via supabase.rpc from apps/web/src/features/finance-enforcement/lib/finance-enforcement-api.ts:484 (frontend-triggered), though it remains the finance-maintained, aging-driven hold system the rental gate ignores.
findings.title: Split-brain credit holds: rental checkout gate reads ar_credit_blocks (no automated writer) and ignores the finance-maintained qrm_companies.credit_hold
findings.detail: The L0 checkout security trigger blocks on_rent only on active ar_credit_blocks rows. But ar_credit_blocks (mig 168) has no automated producer anywhere — no cron, no trigger from invoice aging, no edge-function insert (the only code references are the apply_ar_override RPC and a read in HealthScoreDrawer.tsx:149). Meanwhile the real, automated credit-hold system (evaluate_credit_holds, mig 657) writes qrm_companies.credit_hold from customer_invoices aging — and nothing in the entire L-stream (migs 770-779, rental-ops, portal-api) reads that column. The 'rental_credit_hold' exception source whitelisted in mig 772 has zero producers. Net effect: a customer 90 days past due (finance hold set) can still take a unit on rent, while the gate that should stop them checks an effectively empty table.
findings.recommendation: Make the checkout gate also check qrm_companies.credit_hold (or have evaluate_credit_holds materialize/clear ar_credit_blocks rows so both systems share one source of truth), and enqueue the rental_credit_hold exception when a checkout is blocked.

findings.verdict_correction: Directionally and substantively correct; minor cite fixes: the tax hardcode/metadata spans rental-billing-runner/index.ts:159-173 and the next_rental_invoice_number RPC call is at lines 125-128 (not 118). The FL rental tax machinery (rental_contracts.tax_sourcing_method, rental_invoices.tax_breakdown/dr15 columns, qep_resolve_fl_tax_jurisdiction) lives in migration 666_finance_foundation_county_tax_rentals.sql, which extends mig 656's surtax foundation to rentals. The runner's inline comment shows the tax gap is a knowing deferral ('rate resolution delegates to the jurisdiction machinery when the workspace profile is configured'), not an accidental omission — but no such resolution path exists anywhere in code, so every rental invoice posts with tax_cents = 0.
findings.title: Rental billing bypasses the finance-foundation tax engine — every rental invoice posts with tax_cents = 0
findings.detail: rental-billing-runner hardcodes tax_cents: 0 and total_cents = subtotal, tagging metadata tax_profile: 'workspace-unresolved'. It never calls the tax-calculator edge fn or the FL county discretionary-surtax machinery (mig 656) that finance-enforcement uses for sales invoices — even though finance-enforcement-api.ts itself lists 'Florida county tax destination sourcing and DR-15 rental evidence' as a K1.1 obligation and rental_contracts already carries tax_sourcing_method. Rental invoices also mint numbers from their own global sequence (next_rental_invoice_number, mig 776) instead of the branch-prefixed invoice_number_sequences (mig 655) whose UI explicitly offers a 'rental' department type.
findings.recommendation: Have the billing runner resolve tax through the shared tax-calculator (using the contract's tax_sourcing_method and branch/ship-to county) before posting, and pull invoice numbers from invoice_number_sequences with invoice_type='rental' so rental paper matches the K1.1 numbering and DR-15 evidence contract.

findings.verdict_correction: Two detail refinements: (1) signals can also appear without a manually tagged deal if a voice capture for the company extracted rental_first/rent_to_own/quote_ready data (rental-conversion.ts lines 135-180), so the gate is "manual deal-equipment tag OR voice-capture signal," not deal tags alone; (2) system-wide the RPO accrual is not fully invisible — the flow engine emits a rep nudge when rpo_credit_accrued_cents crosses 50% of purchase price (supabase/functions/_shared/flow-workflows/rental-lifecycle-flows.ts:219-230), but that is a separate task surface and never feeds the Rental Conversion Engine board.
findings.title: Rental Conversion Engine scores rent-to-own candidates while reading zero rental tables
findings.detail: The account-level 'Rental Conversion Engine' (sales surface for converting renters to buyers) builds its signal board from crm_deals, crm_deal_equipment role='rental' links, voice_captures, and service-job customer_invoices — none of rental_contracts, rental_invoices, rental_contract_lines, or rpo_credit_accrued_cents. A customer with months of real on-rent history, paid rental invoices, and accrued RPO credit shows no conversion signal unless someone manually tagged a CRM deal with a rental-role equipment link. The actual rental trunk (dual-anchored on qrm_company_id since mig 769) is fully queryable by company but unused here.
findings.recommendation: Rebuild the board's query over rental_contracts/rental_invoices filtered by qrm_company_id (contract count, trailing rental spend, active RPO accrual, utilization of rented classes) and rank conversion candidates on real rental economics, deep-linking each signal to a pre-filled deal or RPO conversion action.

findings.verdict_correction: Two framing corrections. (a) The claim omits that a designed alternate billing path exists: the L5 final rental invoice is supposed to carry the damage charge (shared/rental-billing-core.ts:165,174 gates damage_charge_cents on damage_disposition='customer_billable', and rental-billing-runner/index.ts:182-199 mirrors it to a properly-attributed customer_invoices row; blueprint in 768_qep_stream_l_rental_department.sql:63 states 'renter_fault_billable → charges on final invoice AND auto-open service_jobs'). The service-job invoice being empty is therefore partly by design (avoids double-billing) — but the path is broken anyway because nothing ever populates rental_returns.damage_charge_cents (the UI writes the legacy dollars column charge_amount instead), so the final invoice bills $0 damage. (b) 'Stuck at work_order_open' is slightly overstated: RentalReturnsPage.tsx:448,539-548 offers a manual 'Finalize damaged return' button that force-patches status to 'completed' from work_order_open — the loop can be closed manually, just never automatically and never in response to the service job closing.
findings.title: Renter-fault damage work order is a billing orphan: no customer, no quote, no rental backlink, and the loop never closes
findings.detail: rental-ops `dispose_damage` (index.ts:906-929) opens the renter-fault service_job with machine_id only — no customer_id, even though the contract carries qrm_company_id/portal_customer_id, and no rental_contract_id/rental_return_id backlink (only rental_returns.work_order_number stores the job id as text, one-way). generateInvoiceForServiceJob (service-invoice.ts:13-25, 42-48, 111-120) requires an approved quote with customer-billable lines and resolves the customer from job.customer_id — so the damage job either produces no invoice or a customer_invoices row with BOTH portal_customer_id and crm_company_id null. Nothing seeds the quote with the assessed charge_amount, and nothing updates rental_returns (stuck at status='work_order_open') when the service job closes — no trigger or function consumes work_order_number.
findings.recommendation: In dispose_damage, resolve the contract's qrm_company_id/portal_customer_id and set service_jobs.customer_id; add a rental_return_id uuid column on service_jobs (or a proper FK) and a trigger on service_jobs.closed_at that advances rental_returns from work_order_open. Decide the single billing path (fold into the rental final invoice OR service invoice) and guard the other to prevent double-billing once both are fixed.

findings.verdict_correction: Minor detail refinements only: the fault-to-signal conversion spans index.ts:168-218 (the ingestSignal call ends at 218, not 206), and the hours-based path is weaker than stated — equipment.hours_crossed_interval is never emitted by any code in the repo, so the 'service_prompt' crm_activities task cannot actually be created today. findings.title: QRM pipeline board hydration re-runs stages + approval-enrichment queries for every 500-row page, sequentially
findings.detail: useOpenDealsHydration loops `await listCrmOpenDealsForBoard({limit: 500, cursor})` page-by-page until all open deals are in memory. Each call to listCrmOpenDealsForBoard first awaits listCrmDealStages() (redundant after page 1), then the deals page, then awaits enrichDealsWithPendingQuoteApprovals() (a quote_approval_cases .in() query). So a workspace with N pages of open deals performs 3N strictly sequential round trips on the QRM pipeline board -- the hot path explicitly called out in CLAUDE.md -- and ultimately holds every open deal in component state.
findings.recommendation: Fetch stages once and pass them into the pager (or filter open deals server-side in the crm_deals_rep_safe view), batch the pending-approval enrichment once after hydration instead of per page, and consider fetching 2-3 pages in parallel or capping full hydration behind virtualized server-side pagination.

findings.verdict_correction: analytics_events is indeed the system-wide event spine with zero retention, pruning, or partitioning — no DELETE/TRUNCATE/partition/retention cron exists anywhere for it, so storage, full-table btree indexes (016:29-34, 049:13-14, 194:50-52), and autovacuum cost grow without bound. But the hot paths are already query-bounded: flow_pending_events limits to a 7-day window over a partial index of unconsumed events (which the runner drains even for unmatched events), and the rental scanners' 20-hour dedup NOT EXISTS is an indexed occurred_at range scan. So the risk is unbounded storage/index bloat and eventual operational cost, not direct latency degradation of the 15-minute paths as table age grows. Also, migration 011 is not the only scheduled cleanup — 528 schedules billing-queue-purge (30-day purge) and 202 schedules iron-memory-decay-nightly — but none of them cover analytics_events.
findings.title: analytics_events is the system-wide event spine with zero retention, pruning, or partitioning
findings.detail: Every flow-engine event, rental lifecycle event, and frontend analytics event lands in public.analytics_events via emit_event() (INSERT in 196_flow_engine_audit_fixes.sql:333-350), including the rental fabric triggers on rental_contracts/lines/returns/invoices (775) and the 15-minute rental_lifecycle_scan cron plus daily rental_intelligence_scan, which each add up to one event per candidate contract per 20h window. A repo-wide grep finds no `DELETE FROM public.analytics_events`, no TRUNCATE, no pg_partman/native partitioning, and no retention cron anywhere (the only scheduled cleanup in migrations is rate_limit_log in 011). The table is not archival-only: it is the flow-runner's poll source (flow_pending_events view) and the dedup source for all rental scanners, so unbounded growth directly degrades hot paths that run every 15 minutes.
findings.recommendation: Add a nightly retention cron (e.g. delete or archive consumed flow events older than N days, keep a tiered audit copy if needed) and/or convert analytics_events to a monthly-partitioned table so scanner and runner scans stay bounded.

findings.title: Rental scanner dedup anti-joins on analytics_events have no matching index
findings.detail: rental_lifecycle_scan() (pg_cron every 15 minutes) and rental_telematics_overage_check() (daily) run a NOT EXISTS per candidate contract filtering analytics_events on flow_event_type + entity_id + occurred_at (775:231-234, 251-255, 274-277, 292-295; 778:320-323). No index covers this shape: idx_ae_flow_event_type is (workspace_id, flow_event_type, occurred_at) — workspace_id is not in the predicate so the prefix is unusable; analytics_events_entity_idx is (entity_type, entity_id) — entity_type is not in the predicate. The planner falls back to the occurred_at index and re-scans the entire trailing-20-hour event window once per candidate contract, 4 loops per tick, 96 ticks per day, growing linearly with total event volume.
findings.recommendation: Add a partial index: CREATE INDEX ON public.analytics_events (flow_event_type, entity_id, occurred_at DESC) WHERE flow_event_type IS NOT NULL — or add entity_type to the scanner predicates so the existing (entity_type, entity_id) index applies.

findings.title: Migration 773 per-row rollup trigger fires a full trigger cascade on every rental line write
findings.detail: trg_rental_lines_rollup (773:178-183) is FOR EACH ROW on INSERT, UPDATE OF status, and DELETE of rental_contract_lines. Each firing does a rental_contracts lookup plus rental_contract_rollup_lifecycle(), which aggregates ALL lines of the contract (772:75-117). An N-line insert or bulk return-coding pays N aggregate scans, and any resulting UPDATE of rental_contracts cascades through five more triggers: the transition guard (773:37-133), the close-billing gate (776:148-152), set_updated_at (235:166), hold maintenance (774:164-168) — which per hold row runs rental_recompute_equipment_fleet_state and updates qrm_equipment — and the event emitter (775:74-78). The trigger also fires on line INSERTs into draft/quoted contracts where the rollup can never apply (it only acts when the contract is on_rent/off_rent), so the counter's normal contract-building flow pays the aggregate for nothing.
findings.recommendation: Convert to a statement-level trigger using transition tables (REFERENCING NEW TABLE) that computes the rollup once per distinct contract per statement, and add a cheap precondition (skip when TG_OP = 'INSERT' and the contract is not on_rent/off_rent) before calling the aggregate function.

findings.title: rental_contract_lines equipment probes cannot use the only equipment index (workspace_id prefix mismatch)
findings.detail: The only equipment-keyed index on rental_contract_lines is idx_rental_contract_lines_equipment_status on (workspace_id, equipment_id, status) (522:360-362). But two hot code paths filter by equipment_id WITHOUT workspace_id, making the index prefix unusable: (1) rental_availability_calendar's per-cell EXISTS `l.equipment_id = e.id AND l.status IN (...)` (774:318-323), executed once per unit per day across up to 93 days of the calendar grid; (2) rental_recompute_equipment_fleet_state `WHERE l.equipment_id = p_equipment AND l.status IN (...)` (774:370-374), which runs inside the trg_rental_holds_fleet_state row trigger on every hold insert/status change/delete. Both degrade to sequential scans of rental_contract_lines as the lines table grows.
findings.recommendation: Add CREATE INDEX ON public.rental_contract_lines (equipment_id, status) WHERE equipment_id IS NOT NULL AND deleted_at IS NULL, or add the workspace_id filter to both queries so the existing index applies.

findings.title: Chat evidence retrieval runs its four independent stages strictly sequentially
findings.detail: In the chat handler, embedQuery (OpenAI HTTP call, line 2317), retrieveDocumentEvidence (line 2338), buildCustomerContextEvidence (line 2359), and searchCrmBroadly (line 2372) are awaited one after another. Document retrieval, context-ID retrieval, and broad CRM search are mutually independent (only retrieveServiceKnowledgeEvidence at line 2397 consumes crmEvidence), and searchCrmBroadly/buildCustomerContextEvidence do not use the embedding at all, so they could start before embedQuery returns. retrieveDocumentEvidence additionally makes a synchronous OpenAI rerank call per keyword candidate (rerankKbEvidence, 20s timeout) inside its loop. Every chat message pays the sum of all stages before the first model token.
findings.recommendation: Kick off embedQuery, buildCustomerContextEvidence, and searchCrmBroadly with Promise.all (or allSettled to preserve per-stage degradation), have retrieveDocumentEvidence await the embedding promise internally, and only serialize retrieveServiceKnowledgeEvidence behind the merged CRM evidence. This removes 2-3 full network stages from every chat turn.

findings.title: crm-router universal search executes 5 PostgREST queries sequentially
findings.detail: crmSearch in crm-router-service.ts awaits the companies (line 187), contacts (line 213), deals (line 243), equipment (line 276), and rentals (line 326) queries one at a time. The five queries are completely independent (different tables, same filters), so the header search bar — GET /qrm/search, the single hottest interactive route in crm-router/qrm-router — pays 5x round-trip latency instead of 1x.
findings.recommendation: Run the five entity queries with Promise.allSettled (rentals already tolerates errors) and merge results afterward. Same output, ~5x less wall-clock latency on every keystroke-driven search.

findings.title: Chat document retrieval loads up to 500 full documents (raw_text) into memory per message
findings.detail: retrieveDocumentEvidence's identifier path selects id, title, raw_text for up to 500 published documents (chat/index.ts:685-691) and does substring matching in JS whenever the message contains an identifier-like token; the lexical fallback repeats this with 150 full documents (lines 824-830). raw_text is large enough that the code later truncates it at 50,000 chars, so this is a multi-megabyte corpus transfer + O(docs × identifiers) JS scan on the chat critical path, repeated on every qualifying message with no caching.
findings.recommendation: Push identifier and lexical matching into Postgres (ILIKE/trigram or tsvector index over title + a normalized identifier column, or reuse the existing chunks table) and select only id/title/excerpt. Never ship raw_text for the whole corpus to the edge function.

findings.title: Realtime subscriptions target tables that are not in the supabase_realtime publication — dashboard and quote-approval realtime is dead weight
findings.detail: Only migration 245 ever adds tables to the realtime publication, and it adds exactly two: parts_requests and parts_request_activity. useDashboardRealtime subscribes to postgres_changes on crm_deals, prospecting_kpis, demos, trade_valuations, crm_equipment, manufacturer_incentives, qrm_predictions, follow_up_touchpoints, deposits, equipment_intake, and rental_returns — none published. Worse, crm_deals and crm_equipment became compat VIEWS in migration 170 (real tables renamed to qrm_deals/qrm_equipment), and views can never be in a publication. useApprovalBypass subscribes to quote_approval_cases (also unpublished), despite its comment claiming it 'replaces poll-style latency'. Result: 5 dashboard pages (OwnerDashboardPage, IronManagerDashboard, IronAdvisorDashboard, IronWomanDashboard, IronManDashboard) each open a websocket channel with 3–7 bindings that will never deliver an event, and the app silently degrades to refetchInterval polling while paying channel-join overhead per client.
findings.recommendation: Fix realtime-tables.ts to reference qrm_deals/qrm_equipment, add the needed tables to supabase_realtime in a migration, and add workspace-scoped filters to each postgres_changes binding so one workspace's writes don't invalidate every client. Alternatively delete the dead subscriptions and rely on the existing polling.

findings.title: Follow-up reminder dispatcher cron silently never registers — '10 minutes' is not valid pg_cron schedule syntax
findings.detail: Migration 046 registers 'crm-dispatch-follow-up-reminders' with the schedule string '10 minutes'. pg_cron accepts standard 5-field cron expressions or '[1-59] seconds' — '10 minutes' raises a parse error, which the surrounding DO block catches with 'when others => raise notice', so the migration succeeds and the job is simply never scheduled. No later migration re-registers it (309_cron_legacy_rewrite rewrites 7 other jobs but not this one). The dispatcher itself is well-batched (limit 75 per run), but the batching is moot if the cron never fires: due follow-up reminders in crm_reminder_instances are only marked fired and delivered as in-app notifications when this function runs.
findings.recommendation: Ship a migration that unschedules any stale job and re-registers with '*/10 * * * *'. Verify against live cron.job that the job exists, and consider making the registration block fail loudly (or log to a table) instead of swallowing scheduling errors.

findings.title: No commission engine — plans, accruals, and rep payout statements are absent everywhere
findings.detail: Commission is the sales rep's daily scoreboard and it does not exist. The Floor widget 'sales.commission-to-date' is titled 'Commission source' and self-describes as 'Closed quote value that will feed commission once QA-R2 defines rules' (floor-widget-registry.tsx:366-372); Deal IQ ships commission as 'status-only until a signed commission-dollar plan feed exists' (migration 712 closeout); the only commission table in the schema, rental_contract_commissions (migration 530), has zero readers or writers outside database.types.ts. The only roadmap trace is E5.2 'QA-R2 Rylee commission deep dive — commission calc spec, widget wireframe', a not_started discovery session — there is no build item for plan storage, accrual, split handling, or rep statements.
findings.recommendation: Build commission_plans + commission_accruals tables keyed to invoiced/funded deals, a rep-facing earnings statement page in the sales companion, and feed the existing Deal IQ commission-readiness slot with real dollars. Include split-commission and departed-rep rules already raised in QEP-QUOTE-PROCESS-TIER-2 DP 1.4 so QA-R2 becomes a config session, not a blocker.

findings.title: No whole-goods procurement or unit cost ledger — equipment enters inventory without PO, landed cost, or floor-plan tracking
findings.detail: vendor_purchase_orders (migration 347) and the AP 3-way match (665: vendor_invoices ↔ POs ↔ goods_receipts) are parts-scoped; no purchase order, receiving, or invoice-match path exists for equipment units. qrm_equipment.current_cost_cents — commented 'for equipment margin and floorplan reporting' (474:70) — has zero writers in supabase/functions or apps/web, so unit cost is never populated, which is why the quote builder falls back to estimated dealer cost (unitPrice*0.8). Floor-plan financing, the dominant carrying cost driving equipment-dealer aging decisions, exists only as a finance_foundation_config key label 'Floor-plan lender terms' (finance-enforcement-api.ts:247) — no per-unit lender schedule, curtailment dates, interest accrual, or payoff-on-sale. The intake kanban's 'Purchase & Logistics' stage (077) carries no cost fields.
findings.recommendation: Add equipment_purchase_orders + receiving that write landed cost (invoice + freight + prep + recon from H10 internal jobs) into qrm_equipment.current_cost_cents, and a floor_plan_liabilities table (lender, curtailment schedule, accrued interest, payoff trigger on sale). Feed true cost into quote margin math and surface days-on-floor-plan interest in the Inventory Pressure Board and aging widgets.

findings.title: Accepted trade-ins never become inventory units — no trade-to-stock conversion workflow
findings.detail: When a deal with a trade closes, the traded machine vanishes: no code converts qb_trade_ins/trade_valuations into a qrm_equipment stock unit. Migration 766 records disposition intent ('pending','inventory','retail','wholesale','auction' at line 357) and gates recondition margin, but stops at an approval audit row — it never creates the unit, assigns a stock number, sets cost basis from trade allowance, or enqueues the machine into the equipment_intake recon pipeline. Grep across supabase/functions finds no file that both reads trade tables and inserts into qrm_equipment. The dealership's primary source of used inventory therefore requires manual re-keying, with no cost lineage from the deal that acquired it.
findings.recommendation: On deal close with a keep-disposition trade, auto-create a qrm_equipment row (ownership='owned', condition from the trade walkaround, cost basis = trade allowance) linked back to the source deal, and enqueue it into equipment_intake for reconditioning — with recon service-job costs accruing onto the unit via the existing H10 internal-cost seam.

findings.title: Customer statements and finance-charge assessment are dead schema — no statement run, document, or late-charge computation
findings.detail: Monthly statements are how equipment-dealer customers actually pay, and they cannot be produced. ar_statement_runs (migration 448) has zero writers in supabase/functions; run_ar_dunning_cycle exists but is invoked only from a manual button in finance-enforcement-api.ts with no pg_cron registration; nothing renders or emails a statement document. Finance charges are configured but never computed: qrm_companies.assess_late_charges (472), finance_charge_basis and florida_finance_charge_lawful_cap config keys (finance-enforcement-api.ts:205-212) have no assessor job anywhere, so Net-30/60 terms carry no consequence beyond a credit hold.
findings.recommendation: Add a monthly statement cron honoring workspace_settings.ar_statement_day_of_month that writes ar_statement_runs, renders a per-customer statement PDF (reusing the quote PDF pipeline), emails it via the existing dunning/M365 plumbing, and runs a finance-charge assessor capped by the FL lawful-cap config. A moonshot layer: let Iron draft collection outreach per aging bucket for human-gated send via email_drafts.

findings.title: deal_timing_alerts has no FK to deals or CRM companies — timing intelligence is stranded
findings.detail: deal_timing_alerts.customer_profile_id references customer_profiles_extended, which has no uuid link to qrm_companies/qrm_contacts/qrm_deals; the only bridge is a fragile three-hop TEXT match on hubspot_contact_id. Migration 207 explicitly deferred deal_timing_alerts out of the deal_signals view for this reason, so timing alerts never appear on the deal record, pipeline badges, or command center. The Moonshot-1 engine computes alerts nobody sees in deal context.

findings.title: CRM write path publishes zero deal lifecycle events to the flow bus
findings.detail: crm-router createDeal/patchDeal (including stage transitions and closed_won) never call publishFlowEvent — no publisher for deal.created/deal.stage.changed/deal.closed_won exists anywhere, even though flow-synthesize whitelists those event types for AI-authored flows. The flow engine (L4 fabric) can react to rental.* and deal_timing.* events but is blind to the core sales pipeline moving. Any flow definition triggered on deal.stage.changed silently never fires.
evidence: supabase/functions/_shared/crm-router-data.ts (no publishFlowEvent); supabase/functions/flow-synthesize/index.ts:43 whitelists the types; only emitters found: deal-timing-scan, anomaly-scan, nudge-scheduler, follow-up-engine, qrm-command-center

findings.title: Split-brain quote entities: legacy `quotes` table still read (and writable) alongside live `quote_packages`
findings.detail: The mobile sales customer detail (fetchCustomerQuotes) and qrm-quotes-api list/create/update against the legacy `quotes` table (migration 029, crm_deal_id FK), but no edge function inserts into `quotes` anymore — the live quote engine writes quote_packages (087, deal_id FK). Reps on the sales surface see quote lists sourced from a dead table while QrmDealDetailPage reads quote_packages; qrm-command-center must read both to reconcile.

findings.title: Reprice drafts are a workflow dead-end — created but never applicable
findings.detail: price-intelligence creates qb_quote_reprice_drafts from OEM impacts, but the apply endpoint deliberately returns 'Draft apply is intentionally not enabled in Phase 1 core; create/review draft only' and no frontend anywhere loads qb_quote_reprice_drafts (only oem-price-feeds and database.types.ts reference the table). A rep who accepts a price change must manually re-edit the quote in the builder with no carried-over deltas, defeating the pipeline's purpose.
