evidence: supabase/functions/oem-price-feeds/index.ts:1408; grep for qb_quote_reprice_drafts hits only apps/web/src/lib/database.types.ts and supabase/functions/oem-price-feeds/index.ts

findings.title: No rental quoting path — quoting cluster is sales-only despite the sales+rental mission
findings.detail: Rental contracts carry their own draft→quoted→reserved lifecycle and an Iron draft_rental_quote flow (Stream L), entirely disjoint from quote_packages: no shared line items, pricing, approval gates, PDF/send/sign, or win-probability. The quote builder's only rental touchpoint is a 'rental_conversion' availability candidate string; VoiceQuotePage's own example transcript asks for 'a rental conversion path' but scenarios are purchase/finance only. Rent-vs-buy is a headline moonshot move (docs/quote-builder-moonshot-roadmap.md Move 1) with zero plumbing.

findings.title: OEM price impacts invisible inside the quote builder itself
findings.detail: qb_quote_reprice_impacts carry quote_package_id, margin-floor breach, and commission deltas, yet nothing in features/quote-builder references reprice data (grep for 'reprice' in the feature returns zero files). A rep editing or about to send an impacted quote gets margin gates computed from stale prices with no warning banner; impacts surface only on the separate Price Intelligence page and sales Today Feed.
evidence: grep -rln reprice apps/web/src/features/quote-builder returns nothing; impacts keyed by quote_package_id in supabase/migrations/627_qep_oem_price_feed_wave.sql and apps/web/src/features/price-intelligence/lib/price-intelligence-api.ts:53

findings.title: Parts orders never produce invoices — order-to-cash dead-ends
findings.detail: parts-order-manager advances orders to delivered but contains zero invoice logic (no customer_invoices hit in supabase/functions/parts-order-manager/index.ts). The audit-mandated parts_invoice_lines table (m468) has no writers or readers anywhere in functions, frontend, or scripts. The only parts→customer_invoices rows come from the BU Pulse demo backfill, so Parts MTD revenue on the floor dashboard is demo data. Rental (rental-billing-runner) and Service (service-invoice-generator, service-billing-post) both have real billing paths; Parts does not.

findings.title: No parts producer on the flow-engine event fabric; parts-received-for-open-job can never fire
findings.detail: The flagship service handoff workflow triggers on parts.item.received, but no code or migration emits that event: parts-order-manager writes only its private parts_order_events table, no parts table has an emit_event() trigger (rental_contracts got them in m775), and only anomaly-scan/deal-timing-scan/follow-up-engine/nudge-scheduler/qrm-command-center publish flow events. The 'parts arrive → release job from parts_waiting' promise is dead code.

findings.title: Intelligence engines are deployed but unscheduled — autonomy is manual-only
findings.detail: parts-auto-replenish, parts-demand-forecast, parts-reorder-compute, parts-predictive-failure, parts-network-optimizer, parts-predictive-kitter, parts-pricing-autocorrect, and the post-sale-parts-playbook batch path have no cron.schedule in any migration and no UI invoker (only parts-predictive-ai and parts-embed-backfill are invoked from intelligence-api.ts; the pressure script invokes the rest for testing). Table comments in m136/m137/m139 explicitly claim these run 'by cron'. PartsForecastPage even instructs users to 'run the parts-demand-forecast cron' that doesn't exist.

findings.title: Two parallel parts-request systems; service techs cannot reach the companion queue
findings.detail: parts_requests (companion QueuePage, process-parts-request lifecycle) and service_parts_requirements (service-parts-manager/planner) are disjoint entities. No file under features/service references process-parts-request or v_parts_queue; parts_requests.work_order_number and bay_number are free-text with no FK to service_jobs. A tech needing parts for a work order re-enters everything, and fulfillment on one side is invisible to the other.

findings.title: Service lifecycle emits zero events onto the flow bus / event fabric
findings.detail: The flow bus (migration 209) and rental event fabric (775) exist, and the flow engine can OPEN service jobs (open_internal_service_job action), but no service-* edge function or service_jobs trigger ever calls emit_event or writes flow_events. Stage transitions, machine_down flags, comebacks, and job closures are invisible to automation — the Flow Engine cannot react to anything the service department does.
evidence: grep across supabase/functions/service-*/ shows no flow_events/publish usage (only follow-up-engine, deal-timing-scan, anomaly-scan, nudge-scheduler, qrm-command-center use _shared/flow-bus/publish.ts); migrations/775_l4_rental_event_fabric.sql triggers cover only rental_* tables

findings.title: Upsell scanner recommendations evaporate — no bridge to QRM sales
findings.detail: service-upsell-scanner produces pm_overdue / maintenance_schedule / bulletin / repeat_visits recommendations but persists nothing and creates no QRM deal, task, or follow-up. The only consumer is a display block in ServiceJobDetailDrawer (scanUpsell at line 117). Service-detected revenue opportunities die when the drawer closes — a direct miss on the sales+service mission.

findings.title: No PM job generation from service_agreements / maintenance_schedules
findings.detail: service_agreements is a register only, explicitly 'separate from maintenance_schedules, which remain the downstream schedule engine' — but no cron worker or function generates service_jobs from due/overdue maintenance_schedules rows. Advisors must manually re-enter PM work at intake; the upsell scanner reads schedules but only to render text.
evidence: apps/web/src/features/service/pages/ServiceAgreementsPage.tsx:134; only writers of maintenance_schedules are portal-api; no service-* function inserts service_jobs from schedules (grep supabase/functions)

findings.title: Geofence exit seam has no event producer
findings.detail: Migration 778's trg_rental_geofence_exit and the rental-geofence-exit workflow both consume geofence_events inserts, but nothing in the repo ever writes geofence_events: no edge function or cron compares telematics_feeds.last_lat/last_lng against geofences. The table comment in migration 162 says 'Crossings detected by geofence-evaluator cron' — that evaluator does not exist. Theft/unauthorized-move detection for on-rent units is fully wired downstream and dead upstream.
evidence: supabase/migrations/778_l7_predictive_fleet_intelligence.sql (trigger), supabase/migrations/162_geofences_postgis.sql:69 (comment), grep shows no writer in supabase/functions or migrations

findings.title: Counter-anchored rental revenue never reaches AR
findings.detail: rental-billing-runner mirrors rental_invoices to customer_invoices only 'if (contract.portal_customer_id)'. Counter/voice/iron contracts anchored solely on qrm_company_id — the whole point of the L0 refactor — are silently skipped, so their invoices are invisible to AR aging, health scores, and portal pay. customer_invoices remains portal-anchored; the code comment defers to a future 'AR id-space unification' with no ticket wiring.

findings.title: Portal booking bypasses the rate resolver and availability RPCs
findings.detail: portal-api's rentals/book route prices via its own TS resolveRentalPricingEstimate over rental_rate_rules (duplicating rental_resolve_rates precedence logic that can silently diverge — ironic given mig 772 added mismatch detection for exactly this id-space) and checks only crm_equipment.availability='available' instead of rental_check_availability, so a portal booking can double-book against future reservation holds. L3's contract ('counter UI and portal both call them — no client-side availability math') is unmet on the portal side.

findings.title: No fleet-wide equipment list page; SerialFirstWidget 'All machines' links 404
findings.detail: There is no browsable equipment inventory/list route anywhere: App.tsx defines only /equipment/:equipmentId and /qrm/equipment/:equipmentId detail routes plus lens pages (/qrm/iron-in-motion, /qrm/inventory-pressure, /fleet). SerialFirstWidget links twice to /qrm/equipment, which matches no route and falls through to the NotFoundPage catch-all (App.tsx:2985). Operators cannot answer 'what iron do we have' without a serial or a company.

findings.title: equipment-vision inventory cross-reference queries nonexistent columns and fails silently
findings.detail: supabase/functions/equipment-vision/index.ts:284 selects `status, list_price, rental_rate_daily` from crm_equipment; the qrm_equipment schema has availability/daily_rental_rate/current_market_value instead (no status, list_price, or rental_rate_daily). The PostgREST error is discarded via `inventoryResult.data ?? []`, so every vision scan returns zero matching inventory — the 'cross-reference against QRM inventory' promise in the function header never fires, including in the Quote Builder point-shoot-trade flow.

findings.title: equipment_service_intervals and replacement_cost_curves have no writers
findings.detail: Migration 160 built PM-interval countdowns and trade-up cost curves into get_asset_countdowns/get_asset_badges, but nothing inserts rows: repo-wide grep finds the two tables only in migrations (160, DQ audits 164/176/181/184, 384) and database.types.ts — no UI, no edge function, no demo seed. AssetCountdownStack therefore shows only the warranty/5000-hour heuristics, and service-history-driven trade-up scoring degrades to hardcoded thresholds. Service module job completions (service_jobs) never update last_completed_hours.
evidence: supabase/migrations/160_asset_intelligence_rpcs.sql:15,47; grep of supabase/functions + apps/web/src + scripts/demo returns no writers

findings.title: Intake pipeline is a workflow dead-end: stage 8 never updates the equipment record
findings.detail: equipment_intake (077) tracks 8 stages to 'Sale Ready' with only history/updated_at triggers; equipment_id is nullable; nothing sets qrm_equipment.availability, sale_ready_at, or intake_stage when a unit finishes intake. Meanwhile 191's mv_exec_inventory_readiness computes COO metrics (intake_stalled, ready_units) from qrm_equipment.intake_stage/readiness_status — columns no workflow populates (readiness_status is written only by the rental trigger in 769). Exec inventory-readiness numbers are structurally hollow.
evidence: supabase/migrations/077_equipment_intake_pipeline.sql:14,95-121; supabase/migrations/191_command_center_operations.sql:48-53,96-101; grep for intake_stage writers in functions/frontend returns nothing

findings.title: Migration 766 trade-recondition approval gate has no operator UI
findings.detail: record_trade_recondition_manager_approval and qep_trade_recondition_approval_state are granted to authenticated but have zero frontend callers; trade_recondition_approval_audit is never read by any page. The Iron Manager dashboard shows trade_valuations rows the 766 trigger pushed to status='manager_review' (useDashboardData pendingTrades) but offers no approve/reject action, so keep-and-recondition trades dead-end in the queue. FinanceEnforcementPage only mentions 766 as a static 'shipped' evidence string in FinanceFoundationStatusPanel.
evidence: supabase/migrations/766_finance_foundation_trade_recondition_margin_gate.sql; grep of apps/web/src shows record_trade_recondition_manager_approval only in database.types.ts and finance-enforcement-api.ts evidence strings; apps/web/src/features/dashboards/hooks/useDashboardData.ts (pendingTrades)

findings.title: Rental department invisible to every executive/owner/dashboard surface
findings.detail: Stream L shipped rates, reservations, utilization, billing, and event fabric (migrations 768-778), yet no rental metric exists in analytics_metric_definitions, no rental KPI tile on OwnerDashboardPage, and the widget registry declares module type 'rentals' with zero widgets registered. The only rental exposure is a legacy rental_returns query on the Iron Man dashboard and a bare /rentals link in the exec department deck.

findings.title: deposit-calculator edge fn is orphaned with duplicated tier logic
findings.detail: No caller anywhere in the repo (frontend, edge fns, scripts) invokes deposit-calculator; the live deposit path in quote-builder-v2 uses DB RPC calculate_deposit_tier. The owner's tier schedule is now maintained in two places, and the fn's Iron-Woman notification path (crm_in_app_notifications kind='deposit_required') never fires. Delete it or make it the canonical wrapper.
evidence: supabase/functions/deposit-calculator/index.ts; supabase/functions/quote-builder-v2/index.ts:2566 (rpc calculate_deposit_tier); repo-wide grep for 'deposit-calculator' finds only docs and config.toml

findings.title: Document plays and knowledge-gaps backend has zero UI
findings.detail: document-router exposes /plays, /plays/action, /plays/run, /plays/draft (role-gated renewal/amendment/termination/warranty draft flows) and /knowledge-gaps, but the frontend adapter features/documents/router.ts wraps none of them and no component in apps/web calls these paths. The entire plays engine (document_plays rows with recommended_action, projected_due_date, suggested_owner_user_id) is a workflow dead-end — operators can never see or action a play.
evidence: supabase/functions/document-router/handler.ts:408-461 vs apps/web/src/features/documents/router.ts (no plays/knowledge-gaps functions); grep for 'plays/draft|/plays' in apps/web/src returns nothing

findings.title: Twin extraction never runs automatically on new documents
findings.detail: Migration 339 defers the auto-queue trigger/cron to a later slice that never shipped: document_twin_jobs is written only by document-twin itself, and document-twin is invoked only via document-router /twin-rerun (the manual button in Document Center). Documents landing via ingest/sop-ingest never get facts, obligations, or plays until someone manually re-runs the twin, so the obligations graph silently drifts stale.
evidence: supabase/migrations/339_document_twin.sql:9 ('Install a trigger / cron that auto-queues twins. That lives in a…'); only writers of document_twin_jobs are document-twin/service.ts; no cron.schedule for document-plays-run/mark_at_risk_obligations in any migration

findings.title: Brian DM-nudge queue has no dispatcher
findings.detail: DecisionsTriagePage's 'DM nudge' writes {state:'queued'} events into qep_decisions.ai_prep_packet.brian_dm_nudges, but no edge function, cron, or script reads brian_dm_nudges/brian_dm_last_nudge anywhere in the repo. Nudges are queued forever and never delivered — a silent workflow dead-end on the owner-escalation path.
evidence: apps/web/src/features/decisions/lib/triage-api.ts:138-164,393-430; grep -rln brian_dm_nudges over supabase/functions and scripts returns zero consumers

findings.title: Two parallel event backbones; the flow bus is write-only
findings.detail: The Flow Engine uses analytics_events + emit_event (migs 194-196, polled by flow-runner), while migration 209 created a second flow_events table with its own publish/subscribe helpers. Five edge fns publish to flow_events (anomaly-scan, deal-timing-scan, follow-up-engine, nudge-scheduler, qrm-command-center) but nothing consumes it — subscribe.ts is imported only by its own test, and no UI reads flow_events. The cutover promised in anomaly-scan/index.ts (lines 26-27, 'retired at the end of Phase 2 Slice 2.2') never happened, so anomaly.detected events accumulate unread while the real workflow runner listens on a different table.
evidence: supabase/migrations/209_flow_bus.sql; supabase/functions/_shared/flow-bus/subscribe.ts (only imported by subscribe.test.ts); supabase/functions/anomaly-scan/index.ts:559-650; supabase/functions/flow-runner/index.ts:517-520 (polls flow_pending_events over analytics_events)

findings.title: escalation_tickets is a workflow dead-end — nobody ever sees the escalation
findings.detail: escalation-router builds an AI email draft, resolves the target manager, and inserts escalation_tickets + a crm_activities task, and voice-to-qrm dispatches it automatically on detected customer issues. But the email is stored in email_draft_content and never sent, and no page in apps/web lists escalation_tickets — the only web reference is the generated database.types.ts; qrm-command-center only counts them. The manager the ticket was routed to has no surface to act on it.
evidence: supabase/functions/escalation-router/index.ts:309-333; supabase/functions/voice-to-qrm/index.ts:1332; grep of apps/web/src shows escalation_tickets only in apps/web/src/lib/database.types.ts; supabase/functions/qrm-command-center/index.ts:515 (count-only)

findings.title: Portal actions emit zero events into the flow engine
findings.detail: portal-api handles invoice payments, native signatures, rental bookings/extensions/payments, service requests, and parts order submission but contains no emit_event or publishFlowEvent call, so no workflow can react (flagship workflow #10 'Portal payment → internal updates' has been deferred since mig 194). A customer signing a rental contract or paying an invoice produces no internal notification, task, or audit event — staff must poll tables or dashboards.
evidence: supabase/functions/portal-api/index.ts (3,581 lines, zero emit_event/publishFlowEvent matches); docs/QEP-FLOW-ENGINE-IMPLEMENTATION.md §7 spec-compliance row 10 'deferred (portal events not yet wired)'

findings.title: flow_events bus is write-only — five publishers, zero consumers
findings.detail: The 'Day 7 dual-write' flow bus (flow_events table, migration 209) is published to by anomaly-scan, deal-timing-scan, follow-up-engine, nudge-scheduler and qrm-command-center, but _shared/flow-bus/subscribe.ts is imported by nothing except its own test. Meanwhile flow-runner consumes a different table (analytics_events). Two parallel event fabrics exist; one silently accumulates dead rows and the signals published there (e.g. follow_up.touchpoint_due) never trigger anything.

findings.title: Predictive parts suite built but never scheduled or surfaced
findings.detail: parts-predictive-failure, parts-pricing-autocorrect, parts-demand-forecast, parts-network-optimizer, parts-reorder-compute, parts-predictive-kitter and parts-auto-replenish all import cron-auth plumbing (_shared/service-cron-run.ts) but no migration registers a cron for any of them, no frontend feature calls them, and no function invokes them — only the dev pressure harness scripts/parts-service-pressure/run.mjs does. Forecast tables (parts_demand_forecasts mig 137, parts_reorder_profiles mig 136) exist but stay empty in production; the parts feature never sees this intelligence.
evidence: supabase/functions/parts-reorder-compute/index.ts, supabase/migrations/136_parts_reorder_profiles.sql, supabase/migrations/137_parts_demand_forecasts.sql, scripts/parts-service-pressure/run.mjs; zero functions/v1/parts-* URLs in supabase/migrations

findings.title: Rental billing does not reach AR for counter-only customers
findings.detail: rental-billing-runner posts rental_invoices nightly but only mirrors to customer_invoices when a portal identity exists; counter-only contracts record a 'mirror-skip note until the AR id-space unification' per the function header. Rental revenue for walk-in/counter customers is invisible to the AR/dunning/portal stack (migrations 448, 664), creating manual reconciliation work.

findings.title: Operational revenue never posts to the internal GL
findings.detail: gl_accounts/gl_journal_entries/gl_journal_lines (441-443) are written only by the equipment sale reversal path; rental_invoices, service billing rows, and parts invoices have no posting engine into the ledger, and no edge function references ap_bills at all. The Stream K accounting schema is a parallel universe: money becomes 'real' in customer_invoices but never lands in a journal — QuickBooks sync papers over it externally.
evidence: gl_journal_entries referenced only in supabase/migrations/442,443,536,540 and supabase/functions/_shared/crm-router-data.ts; zero grep hits for ap_bills under supabase/functions/

findings.title: Two parallel parts inventory spines
findings.detail: Migration 671 creates the Stream G normalized foundation (parts, parts_stock, parts_locations, parts_bins) explicitly 'without replacing the existing parts_catalog / parts_orders / parts_inventory / fulfillment spines'. 11 edge functions read parts_inventory (itself created inside a SERVICE migration, 108); zero read parts_stock. Stock truth is forked — cycle counts and transfers (674/678) operate on the spine the operational functions ignore.
evidence: supabase/migrations/671_phase3_parts_schema_foundation.sql header; supabase/migrations/108_service_tat_inventory_planner.sql line 53; grep: 11 function dirs match parts_inventory, 0 match parts_stock

findings.title: Frozen crm_* compat views are still the primary edge-function API
findings.detail: Migration 170 called the compat views 'temporary scaffolding', yet ~600 migrations later edge functions make 108 from("crm_deals") and 42 from("crm_equipment") calls. Because simple views don't surface columns added post-rename, all fleet-state columns L0 added to qrm_equipment (availability, readiness_status, next_available_at — 769) are invisible to every consumer still on crm_equipment, silently splitting the equipment truth.
evidence: supabase/migrations/170_qrm_rename_tables_and_compat_views.sql; supabase/migrations/769_l0_rental_structural_refactor.sql header note 'crm_equipment compat view is frozen'; grep counts over supabase/functions/

findings.title: Parts availability shown to reps in the quote builder reads the legacy inventory table and drops parts_catalog.on_hand
findings.detail: PackageItemSearchDialog renders 'N on hand' for part results (lines 132-151), but the qty comes exclusively from legacy parts_inventory.qty_on_hand (quote-api.ts:2912-2917). The PARTMAST/CDK bulk import — the pipeline that actually loads dealership stock — writes parts_catalog.on_hand (column added in m257:40, written by _shared/parts-import-partmast.ts:116,241), and the quote builder's parts_catalog fallback query does not even select on_hand (quote-api.ts:2998-3003). Iron's tools already handle the dual-source problem (tools.ts checks both catalogs); the rep-facing quoting surface does not, so reps quote parts against stale or missing availability.
findings.recommendation: Select on_hand in the parts_catalog fallback and merge availability from both sources (mirroring Iron's dual-source lookup), then converge on one shared availability view used by quote-builder, parts-companion, and Iron.

findings.title: The governed parts quoting lane (parts_quotes + pricing engine) has no operator surface anywhere in the app
findings.detail: parts_quotes (m414, customer_id -> qrm_companies, salesperson ownership, expiry dates) and its lifecycle actions create_parts_quote / convert_parts_quote_to_order exist in parts-order-manager (index.ts:1256, 1384) with server-enforced pricing via resolveQuoteLineRows -> parts_resolve_priced_line. But grep finds zero callers of those actions in apps/web/src or any other edge function; the only frontend reference to parts_quotes is database.types.ts, and the floor 'Parts drafts' widget (PartsQuoteDraftsFloorWidget, OperationalWidgets.tsx:413) actually lists parts_orders drafts, not quotes. Account 360's open_quotes payload is built from quote_packages only (m173:63-68), so pending parts quotes for a customer are invisible to reps and counter staff alike — the governed lane is dead capability while the ungoverned quote-builder lane is the only reachable way to quote parts.
findings.recommendation: Build a parts-quote screen in parts-companion that calls create_parts_quote / convert_parts_quote_to_order, and add open parts_quotes (with expiry) to the get_account_360 payload so account owners see pending parts quotes next to equipment quotes.

findings.title: Parts price changes never reprice or flag part lines on open sales quotes
findings.detail: The reprice-impact machinery (qb_quote_reprice_impacts via oem-price-feeds) covers equipment models only — oem-price-feeds/index.ts contains zero references to parts_catalog or parts_vendor_prices — and vendor-pricing-portal/index.ts (where vendor price submissions are approved into parts_vendor_prices) contains zero references to quotes. Part lines snapshot list_price at add time into quote_package_line_items with only jsonb metadata linkage (sourceCatalog 'manual' in quote-api.ts), so when a PARTMAST import or approved vendor submission changes a part's price, every open quote carrying that part keeps the stale price with no impact detection, unlike equipment lines.
findings.recommendation: Extend the reprice-impact computation to part-type quote_package_line_items keyed by part_number: when parts_catalog list/cost prices change (import or vendor-submission approval), compute margin deltas into qb_quote_reprice_impacts so the existing PriceIntelligencePage review queue covers parts too.

findings.title: Parts intelligence and predicted plays are absent from every daily rep surface (morning briefing, Today feed, mobile sales)
findings.detail: The Parts Intelligence Engine produces predicted_parts_plays, parts_predictive_kits, and customer_parts_intelligence, consumed by parts-companion pages (PredictivePlaysPage, PostSalePlaysPage, IntelligencePage) and company-level QRM cards (CustomerPartsIntelCard imported at QrmCompanyDetailPage.tsx:34). But the rep's daily workflow never sees any of it: morning-briefing/index.ts has zero parts references, and the entire features/sales module (Today feed, pipeline, customer detail) has zero references to playbooks, predicted plays, or parts intelligence. A field rep visiting a customer gets no cue that a $4k wear-parts window or PM kit opportunity is due on machines they sold.
findings.recommendation: Add a parts-opportunity section to the morning-briefing generator (top predicted plays and due post-sale playbook windows for the rep's assigned accounts) and a Today feed card in features/sales deep-linking to the account's parts tab with a one-tap 'log outreach' action.

findings.title: Machine/customer service history is invisible from deal views and the mobile rep surface; trade valuation ignores in-house service records
findings.detail: Service history is only reachable from the desktop Account 360 company view (get_account_360 returns service jobs; AccountServiceTab renders them) and the equipment Asset 360 page. The deal workflow has none of it: get_deal_composite (086, extended 127) returns deal/stage/contact/company/needs/cadences/demos/deposit/activities but no service data, and QrmDealDetailPage.tsx contains zero service_jobs references. The mobile Sales Companion — the field rep's primary surface — has no service data at all (no service references in CustomerDetailPage.tsx, DealDetailPage.tsx, or sales-api.ts), so a rep walking into a customer with an open or botched work order can't see it. The trade-valuation edge function accepts a manually typed last_full_service string and never queries service_jobs by machine/serial, even when the trade unit is a machine the dealership itself serviced.
findings.recommendation: Extend get_deal_composite to include open/recent service_jobs for the deal's company and linked equipment, add a service section to the mobile CustomerDetailPage (reuse the get_account_360 service block), and have trade-valuation look up service_jobs by matched serial/machine_id to auto-populate service history and repair-cost context in the valuation.

findings.title: The 'equipment hours crossed service interval' workflow can never fire — the event has no emitter
findings.detail: The flagship flow workflow equipment-hours-crossed-interval (create a service prompt task + audit event when telematics reports an interval crossing) triggers on event pattern 'equipment.hours_crossed_interval', and that event is whitelisted in the flow-synthesize taxonomy. But no producer emits it: telematics-ingest and telematics-signal-ingest contain no flow-bus publish/emit calls, and repo-wide the string appears only in the workflow definition and the whitelist. equipment_service_intervals also has no writers (per the equipment cluster, verified against migrations 160/384 which only read it). The proactive PM-prompt chain — telematics hours → service prompt → rep task — is therefore fully defined and permanently dormant, which also feeds findings 3–4 (no PM-driven leads).
findings.recommendation: In telematics-ingest, after updating telematics_feeds, compare new engine hours against equipment_service_intervals (and seed that table from OEM defaults per make/model) and publish equipment.hours_crossed_interval via _shared/flow-bus/publish.ts with an idempotency key of equipment_id+interval, letting the existing workflow do the rest.

findings.title: Service customer communications bypass the QRM comms timeline — reps can't see what service told their customers
findings.detail: Customer-facing service SMS/email goes through a parallel pipeline: rows queued in service_customer_notifications are dispatched by service-customer-notify-dispatch using its own Twilio and Resend calls (Resend send at index.ts:94), and on success it only updates the service_customer_notifications row. It never writes crm_communication_messages, whose only writers are _shared/crm-communication-delivery.ts plus the sendgrid/twilio webhooks that power the QRM communication timeline. The result: a salesperson viewing their account's QRM timeline sees none of the service department's outbound messages (job status, quote approvals, pickup notices), so sales and service talk to the same customer through disjoint channels with no shared record.
findings.recommendation: After a successful Twilio/Resend send, have service-customer-notify-dispatch also insert a crm_communication_messages row (resolving contact/company via the existing _shared/service-customer-recipient.ts logic) so service messages appear in the QRM account timeline; longer term, route service sends through crm-communication-delivery to unify providers, retries, and delivery webhooks.

findings.title: Two parallel parts-request queues with no bridge: companion parts_requests links to jobs by free-text work_order_number and its 'backordered' status is inert
findings.detail: The counter workspace runs on parts_requests (process-parts-request lifecycle, which includes a 'backordered' status at index.ts:65-68) while the shop runs on service_parts_requirements (usePartsQueue in features/service). parts_requests.work_order_number is plain text with no FK (m245:184, written verbatim at process-parts-request/index.ts:173), so marking a counter request 'backordered' or 'fulfilled' can never touch the service job that needs the part, and the companion queue never shows shop demand: grep confirms features/parts and features/parts-companion contain zero references to service_parts_* tables. process-parts-request also never reads or adjusts any inventory table, so a 'pulled/fulfilled' request doesn't decrement stock either.
evidence: supabase/functions/process-parts-request/index.ts:65-68,173 (backordered status; free-text WO; no inventory ops)
apps/web/src/features/parts (no service_parts references in parts or parts-companion features)
findings.recommendation: Add service_job_id (and optionally requirement_id) FKs to parts_requests, resolve work_order_number on create, and propagate status transitions both ways (request backordered → requirement status/ordering note; requirement staged → request ready) so both departments watch one queue state.

findings.title: Parts Intelligence Engine is one-way: it consumes service history but forecasts, kits, and reorder signals never reach service planning
findings.detail: parts-demand-forecast ingests service_parts_requirements (index.ts:179-183) and parts-reorder-compute counts consumed requirements (index.ts:130-134), so service demand feeds the engine. Nothing flows back: parts_predictive_kits (built from service_jobs/customer_fleet by parts-predictive-kitter) are consumed only by features/parts and the QRM PartsIntelligencePage — zero imports in features/service — so an advisor opening a job for a machine with a ready-made predictive kit never sees it; service-intake seeds requirements only from job_codes.parts_template. The service-parts-planner also ignores forecasts entirely (it reads parts_inventory, vendor lead times, and branch edges only). Additionally, reorder-compute counts only status='consumed', so open requirements on already-scheduled future jobs are invisible to replenishment until after the job finishes.
evidence: apps/web/src/features/parts/components/PredictiveKitsCard.tsx (kit consumers are parts/QRM only; none in features/service)
supabase/functions/service-intake/index.ts:110-112 (intake suggests parts from job-code templates only)
findings.recommendation: Surface matching parts_predictive_kits in service intake/job detail (one-click convert kit lines to service_parts_requirements), and extend parts-reorder-compute to add open requirements with need_by_date inside the horizon as committed demand.

findings.title: Rental billed revenue is excluded from exec revenue/margin KPIs and the owner health dial hardcodes rental = 75
findings.detail: revenue_mtd / gross_margin_dollars_mtd / gross_margin_pct_mtd derive solely from closed-won crm_deals via mv_exec_revenue_daily, so nightly-billed rental_invoices revenue (L5) never appears in the CEO/CFO revenue tiles or margin waterfall. The rental-specific utilization metrics (mig 774) do reach the CEO/COO lenses via owner_role-matched definitions, but company-level financials stay rental-blind. Worse, compute_ownership_health_score still hardcodes v_rental_score := 75 ('default 75 until rental utilization data confirmed') in its latest version (mig 384) even though rental_compute_utilization and hourly snapshots now produce the real number — 15% of the owner's headline health dial is a constant.
findings.recommendation: Add posted rental_invoices totals into mv_exec_revenue_daily (union branch) or a parallel rental revenue metric folded into revenue_mtd, and replace the hardcoded v_rental_score with a score derived from the rental_time_utilization_pct_30d / rental_dollar_utilization_pct snapshots that already exist.

findings.title: Disposal and demand-shortfall intelligence (L7) is advisory-only — no handoff into sales or purchasing workflows
findings.detail: rental_disposal_signals correctly joins trailing-365 dollar utilization and service_jobs cost against OEC to recommend 'consider_disposal', and rental_demand_forecasts computes per-category shortfalls — but both render only as read-only cards in the Rental Command Center's Fleet intelligence panel (slice of 4, no buttons). Nothing converts a consider_disposal unit into a sales motion: no used-equipment listing, no qrm_deals/equipment_intake row, no task, no exception. Utilization thus informs a card a rental manager might glance at, not a disposal/sales decision — the fleet-to-sales loop the mission calls for stops at pixels.
findings.recommendation: Add an action per disposal card — 'List for sale' creating an equipment_intake/used-listing row or a draft qrm_deals row linked via crm_deal_equipment, and emit a rental.disposal.recommended event so a Flow workflow can task the sales manager; mirror demand shortfalls into a purchasing/transfer suggestion instead of a static card.

findings.title: Portal-originated rentals bypass the mig 773 check-out inspection gate entirely
findings.detail: checkout_inspection_required defaults to false (mig 773:32). Counter contracts set it true (rental-ops/index.ts:411-412) and Iron sets it true (iron-actions.ts:981), but portal-api's booking insert never sets it and rental-ops `approve_booking` (index.ts:1005-1026) updates the contract to status 'active'/'awaiting_payment' without setting it — so the guard's inspection check (773:98-104) never fires for the whole portal channel. Portal rentals go on rent with no condition inspection, no outbound meter seed (check_out_contract reads the completed inspection's machine_hours at index.ts:746-799), and no damage-evidence baseline for the return.
findings.recommendation: Set checkout_inspection_required=true in approve_booking (or flip the column default to true per the mig 773 comment's stated intent now that the inspection flow exists), and have approve_booking route through the same reserved→on_rent lifecycle guard instead of writing status='active' directly.

findings.title: No preventive-maintenance or turnaround parts demand ever originates from the rental fleet
findings.detail: rental-ops contains zero parts references, and because no turnaround/PM service_jobs are generated at check-in (finding 1) or from meter hours (finding 4), the parts side never sees rental demand: parts-predictive-kitter kits only from existing service_jobs (index.ts:159), and service-parts-planner sources availability from legacy parts_inventory (index.ts:216-228). The consumption plumbing itself works — service_parts_apply_fulfillment_action decrements parts_inventory.qty_on_hand atomically (mig 121) and H10 posting rolls parts cost into rental-unit cost (mig 691:374-379) — but it is only reachable for the rare damage jobs a human disposes. Wear parts for returning rental iron (filters, teeth, tires) are never forecast, kitted, or reserved, so rental turnaround waits on counter re-entry.
findings.recommendation: Once check-in generates turnaround service_jobs (finding 1), extend parts-predictive-kitter to pre-kit rental turnaround jobs from machine_profiles.common_wear_parts, and feed expected return dates from rental_contract_lines into parts-demand-forecast so branch stock anticipates fleet turnarounds.

findings.title: Parts machine knowledge graph (machine_profiles) has no link to qrm_equipment — same machine identity maintained in three disconnected vocabularies
findings.detail: machine_profiles (245:61, unique on workspace/manufacturer/model/year_range_start) and machine_parts_links (261:229, FK machine_id → machine_profiles) form the parts knowledge graph, but there is no FK or bridge table to qrm_equipment; consumers correlate by fuzzy make/model strings (e.g. parts-predictive-kitter builds a `${make}:${model}` patternMap). service_jobs additionally carries free-text machine_make/machine_model beside its nullable machine_id FK (database.types.ts:43911-43913), a third re-entry of the same identity. Any spelling drift ('Cat' vs 'Caterpillar') silently breaks maintenance-schedule, wear-part, and predictive-kit lookups for a physical machine that already has a canonical row.
findings.recommendation: Add machine_profile_id uuid FK on qrm_equipment (backfilled by a make/model/year resolver function), and have service intake copy machine_make/model from the linked qrm_equipment row instead of free text. All parts intelligence then joins by id, not string.

findings.title: parts-predictive-kitter joins service history on nonexistent service_jobs columns, so learned consumption patterns are always empty
findings.detail: parts-predictive-kitter/index.ts:155-161 queries `service_parts_requirements` with embedded `service_jobs!inner ( workspace_id, equipment_make, equipment_model )`. service_jobs has machine_make/machine_model, not equipment_make/equipment_model (database.types.ts:43911-43913), so PostgREST errors on every run; the code destructures only { data } and ignores the error, leaving historicalReqs undefined and the make/model patternMap permanently empty. The service→parts learning loop (kits informed by what techs actually consumed on this model) is silently dead — kits fall back to generic machine_profiles wear parts only. (Compounded by finding 1: the fleet scan itself reads empty customer_fleet.)
findings.recommendation: Rename the embedded columns to machine_make/machine_model, handle the query error explicitly, and prefer keying history on service_jobs.machine_id → qrm_equipment make/model over free-text columns.

findings.title: Two parallel equipment detail pages split capabilities with no cross-link and split the deep-link graph
findings.detail: The same qrm_equipment row renders on two unrelated pages: /equipment/:id AssetDetailPage (get_asset_360 composite, 7 tabs incl. telematics/docs/photos, Iron advisor) and /qrm/equipment/:id QrmEquipmentDetailPage (edit sheet, sale reversal, MachineLifecycleCard — but no service, telematics, or rental data). Neither page links to the other (grep confirms no '/qrm/equipment' href in AssetDetailPage and no '/equipment/' href in QrmEquipmentDetailPage). Deep links split by origin: service pages, fleet map, and dashboards target /equipment/:id while floor SerialFirstWidget, admin action-links.ts:33, and exec alert-actions.ts:32 target /qrm/equipment/:id — so which capabilities an operator gets depends on which module they arrived from, and editing a machine you found via service means manually rebuilding the URL.
findings.recommendation: Merge QrmEquipmentDetailPage's edit/reversal actions into AssetDetailPage as an actions drawer and redirect /qrm/equipment/:id → /equipment/:id (or at minimum add reciprocal header links), so all modules deep-link to one asset command page.

findings.title: The designed cross-department revenue rollup (revenue_attribution) is never fed parts, service, or rental
findings.detail: Migration 149 added customer_profiles_extended.revenue_attribution with the explicit contract 'Revenue by equipment serial: { SERIAL: { parts, service, purchase } }'. The only writer, revenue-attribution-compute, increments only the purchase key from closed-won deal amounts and carries parts/service/rental forward as existing ?? 0 — they are permanently zero. The Nervous System dashboard's 'Revenue by Model' panel that was built on this data ships a permanent empty state telling the user to 'Populate revenue_attribution'. Parts invoices, service billing rows, and rental invoices all exist per company but no job attributes them to serials or customers.
findings.recommendation: Add attribution writers for the other departments: on service invoice post and rental cycle billing, credit the machine serial's service/rental keys; on parts order delivery with a fleet_id, credit parts. Then the Revenue-by-Model panel and per-unit lifetime economics light up with data that already exists.

findings.title: Iron's account brief (summarize_company) omits rental, parts, service, and AR entirely
findings.detail: The summarize_company tool — the conversational 'brief me on <company>' path — bundles only the company row, open deals, activities, and signals. It has no rentals, parts-spend, service-jobs, or open-invoice arms, even though machine-centric summarize_equipment already includes open rental contracts and summarize_rental exists for single contracts, and rental_resolve_context proves the composite pattern works. A rep asking Iron about a customer gets a sales-only answer for an account that may be mostly rental and parts revenue.
evidence: supabase/migrations/777_l6_rental_context_resolver.sql:14 (composite resolver pattern exists for rental contracts)
findings.recommendation: Add open-rentals (rental_contracts by qrm_company_id), parts-spend (coalesced anchor), recent service_jobs, and open customer_invoices arms to summarize_company, mirroring the summarize_equipment partial-visibility pattern.

findings.title: Documents have no customer anchor; rental COI compliance bypasses the Document Center
findings.detail: The documents table has zero company/contact/customer columns, and document_obligations edges use free-text entity types with no FK — so a customer's contracts, COIs, and warranties can never be listed on any account surface, and the document-twin's expiration extraction cannot police anything customer-specific. Rental COI, the most compliance-sensitive customer document, is tracked as bare columns on rental_contracts (coi_received_at/coi_expires_at/coi_document_url text) with no documents-module link, so the coi-expiring scanner works off manually keyed dates rather than extracted facts.
evidence: supabase/migrations/775_l4_rental_event_fabric.sql:268-281 (coi.expiring scan reads only the manual columns)
findings.recommendation: Add nullable qrm_company_id (and optional rental_contract_id) to documents, link coi_document_url to a real documents row, and let document-twin fact extraction populate coi_expires_at so the existing rental.coi.expiring scanner runs on extracted rather than hand-keyed dates.

findings.title: Branch-prefixed invoice numbering is enforced nowhere — every stream mints its own number format
findings.detail: Migrations 655/662 built company-wide-unique branch-prefixed numbering (locked '01-E1000' format, invoice_number_sequences, next_invoice_number(p_invoice_type)) with per-department prefixes including equipment/parts/service/rental. In practice, next_invoice_number is called only from the finance-enforcement web page's generateInvoiceNumber helper. Service invoices are numbered `SRV-<jobId8>` (ad-hoc string), rental uses a separate next_rental_invoice_number RPC (rental-ops:990,1084; rental-billing-runner:118), and equipment/parts create no invoices at all. The finance foundation's numbering discipline therefore governs zero real invoices, and cross-stream numbers can collide with the sequence space.
findings.recommendation: Make next_invoice_number the single numbering authority: call it from service-invoice.ts and have next_rental_invoice_number delegate to it with the rental dept prefix, so all four streams share one auditable sequence per branch.

findings.title: Deposits are three disjoint systems: sales deposits table + Stripe, rental contract fields + ad-hoc invoice, and an orphaned deposit-calculator
findings.detail: Sales deposits flow through the deposits table (quote-builder-v2 via calculate_deposit_tier, reconciled by _shared/portal-stripe-reconcile.ts:141). Rental deposits are entirely separate: rental_contracts.deposit_required/deposit_amount/deposit_status plus an ad-hoc customer_invoices row from rental-ops (portal customers only), applied later as deposit_applied_cents in rental-billing-runner — they never touch the deposits table, Stripe reconciliation, or the tier schedule, so there is no unified 'deposits held' liability view for the owner. A third path, the deposit-calculator edge function, hard-codes the tier schedule and writes deposits/crm_deals but has zero callers repo-wide (grep outside its own directory returns nothing), leaving duplicated tier logic that can drift from the calculate_deposit_tier RPC.
findings.recommendation: Record rental deposits as rows in the shared deposits table (source='rental_contract', FK to the contract) so Stripe reconciliation and a single deposits-held liability query cover both streams; delete or wire up the orphaned deposit-calculator so tier logic lives in exactly one place (the calculate_deposit_tier RPC).

findings.title: Service WIP page fetches every open service job (30+ columns, two joins) unbounded and filters in memory
findings.detail: ServiceWorkInProcessPage's jobsQuery selects all open service_jobs (closed_at is null) with embedded crm_companies and crm_equipment joins and no .limit()/.range(); search, billing-status, and aging filters run entirely client-side over the full result. The summary query does .select('*') on service_work_in_process_summary with no limit. As the service department scales, this list view becomes an unbounded scan on every visit.
findings.recommendation: Add server-side pagination (.range()) with the billing-status/aging filters pushed into the query, trim the select to columns actually rendered, and cap the summary view select or key it by branch.

findings.title: Sales home Today feed loads 500 select('*') pipeline rows to derive a count, a sum, and 3 alerts
findings.detail: useTodayFeed calls fetchRepPipeline, which does v_rep_pipeline .select('*') .limit(500), then computes deals_in_pipeline (length), total_pipeline_value (reduce), and the top-3 cold/cooling deals client-side. The rep landing page therefore transfers up to 500 full-width view rows for three scalar stats, and the co-mounted price-impacts query re-polls every 2 minutes. fetchCustomerDeals repeats the select('*') pattern on the same view with no limit at all.
findings.recommendation: Select only the columns the feed renders, or add a small RPC returning {count, total_value, top_urgent[3]} for the hero stats; give fetchCustomerDeals an explicit column list and limit.

findings.title: Notification bells poll every 30 seconds and fetch up to 500+ rows just to render a badge count
findings.detail: NotificationBell polls countUnseenFeedbackEvents on refetchInterval: 30_000; that function fetches ALL of the user's hub_feedback rows (unbounded) plus up to 500 hub_feedback_events rows, then counts unseen ones in JS -- every 30 seconds, for every user with the brief hub open. QbNotificationBell in the sales header polls its own query every 30s as well (REFETCH_INTERVAL_MS = 30_000).
findings.recommendation: Replace the row-fetch-and-count with a head:true count query or a scalar RPC (count of events newer than last_seen_events_at), and/or switch the badge to a Supabase realtime subscription so 30-second polling can be dropped.

findings.title: Bundle-size guard only measures index-*.js — 70%+ of the startup payload and all route chunks are uncapped
findings.detail: The CI guard (ci.yml:85 runs bundle:check) sums only files matching /^index-.*\.js$/ against a 199,711 B cap. But the actual pre-paint payload is index (183,199 B) + vendor-ui (396,268 B) + vendor-supabase (194,313 B) + vendor-react-query (55,280 B) — the guard covers ~22% of it. Any growth in the vendor chunks or in large route chunks (QuoteBuilderV2Page is already 496,252 B) passes CI silently. Compounding this, chunkSizeWarningLimit was raised to 1600 (vite.config.ts:98) to accommodate react-pdf, so Vite's own warning is suppressed for any chunk under 1.6MB. Lighthouse mobile CI asserts a performance score but is a lagging, noisy signal compared to a byte cap.
evidence: apps/web/dist/index.html (4 preloaded JS assets, only 1 guarded)
findings.recommendation: Extend check-web-bundle-size.mjs to also cap (a) the sum of all modulepreloaded assets parsed from dist/index.html (true startup payload) and (b) a per-chunk max for route chunks with named exceptions for vendor-maplibre and react-pdf, instead of relying on the raised 1.6MB global warning threshold.

findings.title: RentalCommandCenterPage: undebounced search keystrokes re-render a 1,500-line monolith and fire a Supabase query per keypress
findings.detail: The entire rental command center is one component (RentalCommandCenterPage, line 284) with exactly one useMemo (line 498) in 1,498 lines. counterCompanySearch (line 292) is a controlled input (line 867) wired directly — with no debounce — into a useQuery key (lines 455-468), so every keystroke both issues a new ILIKE query against qrm_companies and re-renders the full page JSX, which includes O(contracts x lines) work executed inline in render: per-contract .filter over all contract lines and inspections (lines 962-966, 998), and repeated .filter over the equipment queue per contract card (lines 966, 1156, 1187). QrmCompaniesPage already demonstrates the correct debounce pattern in the same codebase.
findings.recommendation: Debounce counterCompanySearch before it enters the queryKey (copy QrmCompaniesPage's debouncedSearch pattern), hoist the per-contract line/inspection groupings into useMemo keyed on the query data, and extract the counter-rental form into its own child component so its keystrokes stop re-rendering the on-rent board.

findings.title: The Floor home route eagerly bundles every role's widgets into one 185KB chunk
findings.detail: floor-widget-registry.tsx statically imports all widget implementations for every Iron role — manager, advisor, iron-woman, iron-man, parts, owner, plus all floor-native widgets (22+ static imports, zero lazy) — so the FloorPage route chunk is 185,691 B raw / 42,827 B gzip. The registry's own role gating means a parts counter user downloads and parses the owner/manager/advisor widget code (RoleHomeWidgets.tsx alone is 1,280 lines, OperationalWidgets.tsx 1,056) that will never render for them. This is the home surface — the first route after login for operators — so it sits directly on time-to-interactive.
evidence: apps/web/src/features/floor/widgets/RoleHomeWidgets.tsx (1,280 lines, 9 widget exports in one module)
findings.recommendation: Make FLOOR_WIDGET_REGISTRY entries lazy: store component loaders (() => import(...)) instead of components and wrap resolveFloorWidget output in React.lazy/Suspense, or at minimum split widget modules per role so each operator's home chunk contains only their role's widgets.

findings.title: QuoteBuilderV2Page is a 496KB raw / 131KB gzip single-route chunk — the largest non-vendor chunk in the app
findings.detail: The quote builder route compiles to 496,252 B raw / 131,417 B gzip — 2.7x the guarded index entry and larger than vendor-supabase. The driver is useQuoteBuilderV2Orchestrator.tsx (1,124 lines) which statically imports 40+ sibling hooks, the full QuoteBuilderV2PageView tree (desktop AND mobile shells), and shared/qep-moonshot-contracts, so every sub-surface of the builder loads before the first paint of the route. PDF generation is correctly deferred (useQuotePDF.ts:36 dynamic-imports @react-pdf/renderer), but everything else is monolithic. Sales reps opening a quote on mobile pay the full 131KB gzip parse cost even for a read-only view. It also sails under the raised 1600KB chunk warning, so nothing flags its growth.
findings.recommendation: Split the route by device and surface: lazy-load QuoteBuilderV2PageMobileShell vs desktop shell based on viewport, and dynamic-import heavyweight sub-panels (intelligence panel host, wizard chrome, catalog adds) behind their open/expand interactions. Add this chunk to a per-chunk budget once the guard is extended.

findings.title: inspection_runs.rental_contract_id FK has no index but is probed by the checkout guard, the L6 resolver, and the command-center list
findings.detail: 427_inspection_runs.sql creates the rental_contract_id FK (line 20) but only two indexes exist — (workspace_id, service_job_id, ...) and (workspace_id, customer_id, equipment_id, ...) (427:42-51); neither covers rental_contract_id. Three confirmed consumers do per-row lookups on it: the 773 checkout guard's EXISTS on every reserved→on_rent transition when checkout_inspection_required (773:99-104), the L6 context resolver subquery (777:71), and the Rental Command Center's onRentOpsQuery which runs `.in("rental_contract_id", reservedIds)` for up to 100 reserved contracts on every page load / 30s refetch (RentalCommandCenterPage.tsx:643-648). All become sequential scans of inspection_runs, a table shared with service and customer inspections that grows continuously.
findings.recommendation: Add CREATE INDEX ON public.inspection_runs (rental_contract_id, completed_at) WHERE rental_contract_id IS NOT NULL — this serves the guard's completed_at predicate, the resolver, and the list view in one partial index.

findings.title: Availability calendar and demand forecast run O(fleet-or-categories × days) correlated subqueries per call
findings.detail: rental_availability_calendar (774:292-342) CROSS JOINs the rental fleet against generate_series of up to 93 days and evaluates two correlated EXISTS probes (lines + holds) per (unit, day) cell — a 200-unit fleet costs ~18,600 cells and ~37,000 index/seq probes per call, and this is the single availability answer both counter and portal call. rental_forecast_demand (778:100-118, cron daily) repeats the pattern: per category per day over 61 days it runs two correlated count subqueries, and the line-side one includes a per-line NOT EXISTS against rental_reservation_holds (778:113-114). The daily cron cadence contains the forecast cost, but the calendar is an interactive path.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite both as set-based interval overlaps: pre-aggregate the lines and holds for the window once (one scan each), then join to the day series — instead of correlated per-cell EXISTS/count subqueries. Pair with the equipment_id index fix so remaining probes are indexed.

findings.title: rental_reservation_holds.rental_contract_line_id FK is unindexed but used in three NOT EXISTS dedup probes and a CASCADE
findings.detail: 774 creates the rental_contract_line_id FK with ON DELETE CASCADE (774:41) but only indexes equipment/contract/workspace (774:60-66). The column is probed per line in three places: hold creation dedup in the reserved-transition trigger (774:132-135), the category-availability double-count guard (774:276-279), and the daily demand forecast (778:114). Every probe and every rental_contract_lines delete (CASCADE lookup) is a sequential scan of the holds table, which never shrinks because released/converted holds are kept as rows, not deleted.
findings.recommendation: Add CREATE INDEX ON public.rental_reservation_holds (rental_contract_line_id) WHERE rental_contract_line_id IS NOT NULL AND status = 'active' AND deleted_at IS NULL (plus a plain FK index if CASCADE volume matters).

findings.title: flow_cleanup_idempotency() is defined but never scheduled; the wider flow/audit table family has no retention
findings.detail: 196_flow_engine_audit_fixes.sql:360-376 defines flow_cleanup_idempotency() (DELETE FROM flow_action_idempotency WHERE expires_at < now()) with a comment saying to run it 'as part of the same cron tick as the flow-runner', but no cron.schedule in any migration references it and supabase/functions/flow-runner/index.ts never calls it — expired idempotency rows accumulate forever. The same no-retention pattern holds for flow_events (209:96, whose own RLS policy comment anticipates a 'retention prune' that does not exist), flow_workflow_runs/flow_workflow_run_steps (194:109,154, one-plus rows per processed event), geofence_events (162:44+, a telematics stream), service_cron_runs (109:53, one row per flow-runner tick), and analytics_kpi_snapshots — write_kpi_snapshot INSERTS a new row and keeps the old one as 'recalculated' (193:184-198), and 774's hourly cron writes 4 snapshots per workspace per hour (774:644-652).
findings.recommendation: Schedule flow_cleanup_idempotency() on pg_cron (it already exists), and add one consolidated nightly retention job covering flow_events, finished flow_workflow_runs/steps, service_cron_runs, superseded ('recalculated') kpi snapshots, and aged geofence_events.

findings.title: qrm_equipment has no index for the ownership = 'rental_fleet' filter used by every rental surface
findings.detail: All rental fleet queries filter ownership = 'rental_fleet': the hourly rental_snapshot_utilization cron (774:501-506 and the per-workspace loop at 774:636), rental_check_availability category supply (774:255-259), the availability calendar (774:333-337), the 778 forecast/disposal/yield functions, and the Rental Command Center fleet query which loads on every page view with a 120s refetch (RentalCommandCenterPage.tsx:311-315). No index on the table covers ownership — the existing composites are (workspace_id, availability) and (workspace_id, category) (047:75-82) — so each of these degrades to scanning the whole workspace's equipment (sales inventory included) to find the rental fleet subset.
findings.recommendation: Add a partial index: CREATE INDEX ON public.qrm_equipment (workspace_id, category, availability) WHERE ownership = 'rental_fleet' AND deleted_at IS NULL — it serves the fleet list, the category supply count, and the utilization counters simultaneously.

findings.title: Company hierarchy/subtree endpoints fetch up to 5,000 companies per request to walk the tree in JS
findings.detail: fetchCompanySubtreeIdSet and getCompanyHierarchy both select id/parent_company_id (and name) for every non-deleted company in the workspace with .limit(5000), then compute the subtree/ancestors in JavaScript with an O(rows × depth) scan (collectCompanySubtreeIds re-scans the full array per node). getCompanyHierarchy additionally runs its four steps (root lookup, full list, rollups RPC) sequentially. listEquipmentForCompanySubtree (equipment tab with subtree_root) and GET /companies/:id/hierarchy pay this on every load; listContacts with tree_root already uses a paged RPC, showing the RPC pattern exists.
findings.recommendation: Replace the client-side walk with a recursive-CTE RPC (e.g. crm_company_subtree_ids(p_workspace_id, p_company_id)) mirroring list_crm_contacts_for_company_subtree_page, and parallelize the remaining independent reads in getCompanyHierarchy with Promise.all.

findings.title: Chat broad CRM search hydrates each matched contact with ~5 sequential N+1 queries
findings.detail: searchCrmBroadly's initial fan-out is a good 15-way Promise.all (chat/index.ts:1551-1655), but the per-contact hydration loop then runs sequentially for up to 3 contacts: company lookup (line 1705), deals (line 1729), contact activities (line 1759), then a nested per-deal activities loop (lines 1768-1779, 2 more queries), then voice captures. Worst case ~15+ serial round trips appended to every chat message that matches contacts, plus a per-proper-name voice_captures loop at lines 1966-1972.
findings.recommendation: Batch the hydration across all matched contacts: one .in('primary_company_id', ...) company query, one .in('primary_contact_id', ...) deals query, one activities query keyed by contact_id/deal_id arrays, and run the independent groups under Promise.all.

findings.title: GET /qrm/duplicates re-runs a workspace-wide contact self-join on every list read
findings.detail: crm-router's duplicates route calls refreshDuplicates(ctx) by default (refresh must be explicitly 'false') before listing candidates. refreshDuplicates invokes the crm_refresh_duplicate_candidates RPC, which CTE-joins all non-deleted workspace contacts against themselves on normalized email and upserts candidate pairs — a full-table self-join executed synchronously on every elevated user's page view of the duplicates screen, recomputing data that only changes when contacts change.
findings.recommendation: Move the refresh off the read path: run it on contact create/update triggers or a cron (crm-reminder-dispatcher-style), or at minimum debounce with a last-refreshed-at timestamp so repeated GETs within a few minutes skip the self-join.

findings.title: Chat blocks time-to-first-token on telemetry writes after the model stream is already open
findings.detail: After openStreamingCompletion has connected to OpenAI, the handler awaits an insert into retrieval_events (chat/index.ts:2810-2824) and, for empty-evidence turns, a log_knowledge_gap RPC (lines 2827-2838) before constructing and returning the SSE Response at line 2840. These 1-2 DB round trips are pure observability and delay the first streamed token on every message. Relatedly, executeToolCalls runs multiple tool calls from a single model round strictly sequentially (chat-tools.ts:1663-1693).
findings.recommendation: Fire the retrieval_events insert and knowledge-gap RPC without awaiting (or via EdgeRuntime.waitUntil) so the stream Response returns immediately, and execute same-round tool calls with Promise.all in executeToolCalls.

findings.title: embed-crm/embed-qrm pipeline embeds and upserts fully serially across entity types and batches
findings.detail: The embedding job processes the 6 entity types in a sequential for-loop (embed-crm/index.ts:401-462); within each type, batches of 20 run serially — each iteration awaits the OpenAI embedTexts call then the crm_embeddings upsert before starting the next (lines 426-455). Worst case (6 types × 200 records) is ~60 serial OpenAI calls + 60 serial upserts per run. fetchPendingDeals also does its contact/company/stage name lookups as 3 sequential queries (lines 212-232) that are independent, and embed-qrm re-exports this same handler.
findings.recommendation: Run entity types concurrently (Promise.allSettled keyed by type), pipeline batches with a small concurrency pool (e.g. 3-4 in flight), and fetch the deal lookup maps with Promise.all. Freshness of semantic search improves and the function stays well inside edge time limits.

findings.title: qrm-ask-iron tool executors issue 3-4 independent queries sequentially per tool call
findings.detail: Several Ask Iron tools serialize queries that only share the parent-record id: toolGetDealDetail awaits deal, then activities, then signals (qrm-ask-iron.ts:1941, 1959, 1973); toolSummarizeCompany awaits company, deals, activities, signals in sequence (2043, 2063, 2077, 2090); toolSummarizeDay awaits active moves, completed moves, touches, signals in sequence (2852, 2871, 2888, 2897); toolSummarizeContact repeats the pattern (2174-2231). Each tool call inside the Ask Iron chat loop pays 3-4 serial DB round trips, and the loop can run several tool rounds per user question.
findings.recommendation: After fetching the parent record, run the child queries (activities, signals, deals, touches) with Promise.all inside each tool executor. This is a mechanical change that cuts per-tool latency roughly 2-3x.

findings.title: Service workers are double-scheduled: pg_cron jobs and a GitHub Actions cron both fire the same edge functions every 5 minutes
findings.detail: Migrations 097/105/107/114 register pg_cron jobs for service-tat-monitor (*/5), service-stage-enforcer (*/5), service-vendor-escalator (*/15), and service-customer-notify-dispatch (*/10). The repo also ships .github/workflows/service-cron.yml with schedule '*/5 * * * *' that POSTs all four functions with the service-role key. SERVICE_CRON.md calls the workflow a 'fallback when pg_cron is unavailable', but nothing gates it — if the repo secrets are configured (as the sign-off doc implies), tat-monitor and stage-enforcer run 2x every 5 minutes, vendor-escalator up to 4x per 15-minute window, and customer-notify-dispatch up to 3x per 10 minutes. Every extra run is a full scan pass by the worker plus a service_cron_runs audit row, and any non-idempotent side effect (customer notifications, escalations) risks duplication.
findings.recommendation: Pick one scheduler. Either delete the schedule trigger from service-cron.yml (keep workflow_dispatch for manual runs) or have the workflow first check a flag/health endpoint indicating pg_cron ownership before POSTing.

findings.title: rental_lifecycle_scan (every 15 min) and rental_telematics_overage_check dedupe against analytics_events with no usable index
findings.detail: rental_lifecycle_scan runs 4 passes every 15 minutes; each pass has a NOT EXISTS dedupe subquery on analytics_events filtering (flow_event_type = X AND entity_id = Y AND occurred_at > now() - 20h). No index serves this: idx_ae_flow_event_type leads with workspace_id (not in the predicate), analytics_events_entity_idx leads with entity_type (not in the predicate), and analytics_events_event_name_idx indexes event_name, not flow_event_type. The planner falls back to an occurred_at range scan over the last 20 hours of analytics_events — the single busiest table in the system (all UI analytics plus all flow events land there) — repeated for each of the 4 passes, 96 runs/day. rental_telematics_overage_check in 778 (daily via rental-intelligence-daily) uses the identical unindexed pattern. Cost grows linearly with total event volume, not with rental activity.
findings.recommendation: Add a partial index: create index on analytics_events (flow_event_type, entity_id, occurred_at desc) where flow_event_type is not null. Alternatively track last-emitted timestamps on a small dedupe table instead of querying the event log.

findings.title: flow-runner pays a fixed ~30-query overhead every 60-second tick even when idle, and consumes unmatched events one RPC at a time
findings.detail: Every tick, before touching any event, the runner loops over all ~28 REGISTERED_WORKFLOWS, SHA-256 hashes each definition, and issues one SELECT per workflow against flow_workflow_definitions to compare hashes (flow-runner/index.ts:425-493) — roughly 40k no-op queries/day for definitions that only change on deploy. Separately, events whose flow_event_type matches no workflow are marked consumed via an individual mark_event_consumed RPC per event (index.ts:546-555), up to 200 sequential round-trips in a single tick after any burst of unsubscribed events (e.g. every qrm_deals insert emits deal.created whether or not a workflow listens).
findings.recommendation: Sync definitions only when a build hash (computed once per cold start) differs from a stored value, and batch-consume unmatched events with a single UPDATE ... WHERE event_id = ANY(...) instead of per-event RPCs.

findings.title: Write amplification per flow event: each event x matched workflow executes 8-12 sequential DB writes, and row triggers on qrm_deals turn bulk imports into event storms
findings.detail: flow_emit_from_deal fires on every INSERT and every stage change of qrm_deals (194:395-398), so a HubSpot import or demo seed of N deals inserts N analytics_events rows plus N pg_notify calls inside the write transaction. The runner then drains at most 200 events per 60s tick, and executeRun costs per event-x-workflow: run insert, flow_resolve_context RPC, resolved_context update, action_log insert, then per action step a step insert + idempotency select + step update (+ idempotency insert), then run finalize + action_log + mark_event_consumed (flow-runner/index.ts:149-393) — all sequential awaits. A 1,000-deal import produces a backlog that takes 5+ ticks to drain while newer operational events (rental.overdue, quote approvals) queue behind it, since polling is strictly occurred_at ascending with no priority lane.
findings.recommendation: Suppress or coalesce emit during bulk paths (session GUC checked in the trigger, or batch-source events with a single synthetic event), and consider a priority column on flow_pending_events so time-critical rental/service events are not starved behind import backlogs.

findings.title: Parts queue page refetches the entire queue on every parts_requests change from any workspace, with no debounce
findings.detail: QueuePage subscribes to postgres_changes with event '*' on the whole parts_requests table — no workspace, branch, or status filter — and calls refetch() directly in the callback (QueuePage.tsx:332-351). parts_requests IS in the realtime publication (245), so this one actually fires. A bulk sweep (e.g. the stage enforcer or an import touching 50 rows) delivers 50 events to every open client, each triggering a full fetchPartsQueue round-trip, on top of the always-on refetchInterval: 60_000 (line 328). Contrast with useDashboardRealtime, which debounces invalidations by 250ms for exactly this reason.
findings.recommendation: Add a workspace/branch filter to the postgres_changes binding and wrap refetch in a trailing debounce (250-500ms) like useDashboardRealtime does; drop or lengthen the 60s polling interval once realtime is filtered.

findings.title: No payroll bridge — timecards and pay-ladder rates never become a pay run or payroll export
findings.detail: The inputs all exist — service_timecards (161), technician pay-ladder tiers/assignments (642), employees/employee_classes/shift_codes (454-456) — but nothing aggregates hours into a pay period, applies OT rules or ladder rates, or exports to a payroll provider. qrm_payroll_entries (431) is explicitly a payroll *analysis* import table (comment: 'for payroll analysis reports', employee_id kept without FK), not a pay run. Grep finds no payroll_run/payroll_export anywhere, and Stream J shipped only appraisals + ladder progression. The K-stream decision keeps QuickBooks for 'vendor-pay + cash', leaving technician pay with no system path at all.
findings.recommendation: Build a pay-period close: aggregate service_timecards per employee, apply ladder rate + OT/premium codes, produce a reviewable payroll_runs record and a provider export file (ADP/Gusto/QuickBooks payroll CSV) consistent with the K4.1 'QuickBooks as outbound feed' policy. This also makes the shipped pay-ladder raise math actionable instead of a dead-end.

findings.title: No barcode/scan workflow at the parts counter or bins despite a shipped bin schema
findings.detail: Parts counter scanning is DMS table stakes (IntelliDealer counter ops are scan-driven), yet no scanner input exists anywhere: grep for scanner/onScan/scan_sku across apps/web/src/features/parts and parts-companion returns nothing. The only 'barcode' columns in the schema are PDI checklist booleans on equipment_intake (077:44). Stream G shipped parts_bins/parts_locations (671) and cycle counts (678), but counting and picking are typed-search-only — slow and error-prone for high-frequency counter transactions the mission's parts-counter role runs all day.
findings.recommendation: Add camera/HID-wedge scan input to Counter POS fast mode, cycle-count, and fulfillment-pick pages: resolve UPC/OEM barcode → parts_catalog (store a barcode column + alias table), and printable bin labels for parts_bins. Pairs naturally with the existing parts-identify-photo vision lane as a fallback for unlabeled parts.

findings.title: Sales-tax collected is never persisted or reported — no remittance/liability reporting for filing
findings.detail: tax-calculator computes FL county surtax at quote/preview time and migration 666 adds county tax for rentals, but customer_invoices.tax_breakdown (added in 477:16 along with tax_code_1..4) has zero writers across supabase/functions and apps/web — invoices never store what tax was charged, by jurisdiction. There is no sales/use tax liability or remittance report anywhere (FET and Form 8300 got dedicated tables in 660/668; sales tax got nothing), so the controller cannot produce a DR-15-style county filing from QEP even though K-stream declares QEP the reporting system of record.
findings.recommendation: Persist the tax-calculator result into customer_invoices.tax_breakdown at every invoice-creation path (service, rental, parts, and the new equipment settlement), then add a finance-enforcement 'Tax collected' report grouped by county/surtax-cap period for remittance filing, with quarter-close (663) locking the reported periods.

findings.title: Deal Timing module is a navigation and workflow dead-end
findings.detail: /deal-timing is registered only in App.tsx — no nav menu, floor widget, QRM lens, or sales surface links to it. DealTimingAlertCard's 'actioned' button just flips status; it neither creates a deal, links an existing one (actioned_deal_id is never populated from UI), nor opens the pipeline. The scan also hardcodes p_workspace_id='default' on both GET and POST, breaking multi-workspace.

findings.title: Sales mobile mutations bypass the crm-router contract and pipeline gates
findings.detail: sales-api.advanceDealStage updates crm_deals.stage_id directly via PostgREST and ScheduleFollowUp writes crm_deals directly, skipping crm-router's stage validation (VALIDATION_STAGE_CREATE_OPEN_ONLY), deposit/pipeline gates enforced in QRM drag-drop (pipeline-gates.ts), activity delivery locks, and audit. logVisit/createQuickNote/logSalesActivity insert crm_activities directly instead of the router's createActivity. Violates the repo convention that mutation-heavy workflows go through QRM router contracts.

findings.title: Rental event fabric emitted but never consumed by the sales cluster — rent-to-own conversion has no workflow
findings.detail: The rental fabric emits 15+ event types (rental.nearing_end, rental.rpo.threshold_reached, rental.overdue, rental.returned...) yet RentalConversionEnginePage recomputes conversion candidates from raw table scans (crm_deals, crm_deal_equipment, voice_captures, customer_invoices, crm_equipment) and offers no action: no move creation, no signal ingest, no deal creation from a conversion candidate. The moves/signals recommendation loop (crm-router /qrm/moves, /qrm/signals) exists but rental events never feed it.
evidence: grep of rental.* event emitters across supabase/functions; apps/web/src/features/qrm/pages/RentalConversionEnginePage.tsx:43-79; supabase/functions/_shared/qrm-signals.ts (writers are inbound-email/telematics/news adapters only)

findings.title: QRM intelligence lens pages are read-only boards disconnected from the moves loop
findings.detail: The ~15 moonshot lens libs (cross-dealer-mirror.ts, cashflow-weather.ts, white-space-map.ts, competitive-threat-map.ts, etc.) emit rows with only {actionLabel, href} navigation stubs — none create a move, signal, task, or campaign despite the moves API being the designed closure loop (patchMove auto-logs touches and suppresses signals). Insight is computed then dropped; reps must manually re-enter intent elsewhere.
evidence: apps/web/src/features/qrm/lib/cross-dealer-mirror.ts (CrossDealerMirrorRow), apps/web/src/features/qrm/lib/cashflow-weather.ts (CashflowWeatherRow); closure loop exists at supabase/functions/_shared/qrm-moves.ts:346-367 and crm-router/index.ts:999-1036

findings.title: Deal-room customer telemetry doesn't reach the deal timeline
findings.detail: Deal-room concierge chat transcripts, trade-estimate requests (a strong trade-in-interest signal that deal-timing-scan separately tries to infer), and attachment browsing are served by quote-builder-v2 public endpoints but are not written back as crm_activities, signals, or deal_timing inputs — only accept/feedback have writeback (advanceQuoteDealStage, rep_notified). The customer literally telling the concierge what they want never reaches the rep's QRM record.
evidence: apps/web/src/features/deal-room/lib/deal-room-api.ts:279-325 (public-chat, public-trade-estimate have no CRM writeback path); supabase/functions/quote-builder-v2/index.ts:2944-2966 (accept is the only stage writeback)

findings.title: Four parallel quoting engines with duplicated pricing/approval logic
findings.detail: Sales quotes (quote_packages + quote_approval_cases), service quotes (service_quotes/service_quote_lines/service_quote_approvals via service-quote-engine), parts quotes (parts_quotes/parts_quote_lines), and rental 'quoted' contracts each implement separate line items, totals, and approval workflows. No shared line-item model, tax/margin engine, or cross-surface customer quote history — Account 360 past-quotes aggregation only sees quote_packages.

findings.title: Margin waterfall still falls back to estimated dealer cost (unitPrice * 0.8)
findings.detail: computeQuoteWorkspace uses item.dealerCost when present but silently falls back to 80% of unit price, so margin-floor gates and approval triggers can fire on fabricated economics. catalog_entries already stores dealer_cost/cost_to_qep (used by the inventory-first action) but that authoritative cost is not wired into quote line items. Flagged MARGIN-AUTHORITY P1 in the backend plan and still open.

findings.title: Voice/Iron quote handoffs ride on expiring sessionStorage with no server record
findings.detail: Voice scenario selection (10-min TTL) and Iron intake (30-min TTL) hand off via sessionStorage keys; a blocked storage write, expiry, or device switch silently drops the AI-architected scenario (VoiceQuotePage only toasts 'your browser blocked the voice handoff').
