Nothing persists the selected scenario server-side keyed to voice_session_id, so the qb-ai-scenarios output is unrecoverable, and the realtime voice stack (voice-realtime-session, voice-extract-entities) is unused by voice-quote which is batch-only.
evidence: apps/web/src/features/voice-quote/lib/voice-quote-handoff.ts:4; apps/web/src/features/quote-builder/lib/iron-quote-handoff.ts:2; apps/web/src/features/voice-quote/pages/VoiceQuotePage.tsx:613-632; voice-realtime-session only consumed by apps/web/src/lib/voice-realtime-client.ts (VoiceCapturePage, not voice-quote)

findings.title: Retired legacy price lane still wired into the Flow Engine
findings.detail: price-intelligence-api.ts states the price-file-import / requote-drafts CLIENT lane was retired, yet flow-runner still registers the price-file-imported workflow that drives requote-drafts against the old price_change_impact view — two divergent reprice pipelines (price_change_impact vs qb_price_change_events) can produce conflicting drafts and email_drafts for the same quote.

findings.title: Dual inventory truth: parts_catalog.on_hand vs legacy parts_inventory, never synced
findings.detail: CDK PARTMAST import writes stock to parts_catalog.on_hand (_shared/parts-import-partmast.ts), but quote-builder part lines (quote-api.ts:2913), service-parts-planner sourcing decisions (index.ts:216, heuristics literally named parts_inventory_branch_qty), and useInventoryHealth all read the legacy parts_inventory table. Nothing reconciles the two; Iron's lookup_part has to query both and can return conflicting availability.

findings.title: Post-sale playbooks and predictive plays invisible to sales reps
findings.detail: QEP-Parts-Intelligence-Module-Complete-2026-04-16.md promised 'sales reps see your customer has 3 open playbooks worth $2,400 when they open a deal', but post_sale_parts_playbooks and predicted_parts_plays are consumed only inside parts-companion (post-sale-api.ts, intelligence-api.ts) and by owner-ask-anything — no QRM deal page, company page, or sales-companion surface references them. The revenue-forward pipeline never reaches the people who would send it.
evidence: grep post_sale_parts_playbooks / predicted_parts_plays across apps/web/src — only parts-companion + database.types hits; QEP-Parts-Intelligence-Module-Complete-2026-04-16.md:138

findings.title: Replenish approval never creates a purchase order — manual re-entry into vendor_purchase_orders
findings.detail: mark_replenish_ordered (m267) flips queue rows to 'ordered' and stores a free-text po_reference; it does not insert into vendor_purchase_orders even though a full PO module exists at /parts/purchase-orders (m347, PurchaseOrdersPage). An operator approving replenishment must separately hand-create the PO and retype the reference, and supplier fill-rate scoring (v_supplier_fill_rate) relies on queue lifecycle alone.

findings.title: customer_parts_intelligence is stale-by-construction, yet drives QRM and floor surfaces
findings.detail: Its only writer is parts-network-optimizer, which has no cron and no UI/edge invoker (only the pressure-test script and demo seed touch it, and m767 purges the demo rows). CustomerPartsIntelCard on QRM company/account pages and the floor customer-intel widget therefore render frozen or empty data while presenting it as live intelligence. Same staleness applies to parts_predictive_kits (parts-predictive-kitter) and parts_transfer_recommendations (parts-network-optimizer).

findings.title: Rental damage work-order loop never closes
findings.detail: rental-ops sets rental_returns.status='work_order_open' and stores the service job uuid in work_order_number, and the L3 trigger restores equipment readiness when the job closes — but nothing updates rental_returns when its linked service_job closes. Returns stay 'work_order_open' forever unless manually edited; rental ops can't see repair completion.
evidence: supabase/functions/rental-ops/index.ts:930-937 (only writer); no trigger/function in supabase/migrations or functions updates rental_returns from service_jobs state (grep 'update public.rental_returns')

findings.title: SOP suggestions and executions unused in service surfaces despite backend support
findings.detail: sop-suggest explicitly maps entity types service_job, equipment_intake, parts_order to departments (index.ts:44-50, docstring says 'called from deal detail, service pages, intake pages'), but SopSuggestionWidget/SopNudgeInline are embedded only in QRM deal surfaces, and fetchActiveSopExecutionForContext hard-types contextEntityType to 'deal'. Technicians and intake advisors never see SOP nudges; sop_executions are never linked to service jobs.
evidence: supabase/functions/sop-suggest/index.ts:44-50; apps/web/src/features/sop/lib/sop-api.ts:799-801; grep shows widget embeds only in features/qrm/pages/QrmDealDetailPage.tsx:741 and features/qrm/components/PipelineDealCard.tsx:115

findings.title: Appraisal raise math and pay-ladder eligibility are workflow dead-ends
findings.detail: Finalized appraisals compute recommended_raise_pct and the pay ladder computes eligible_for_next_tier from live service metrics, but neither writes to technician_pay_ladder_assignment.hourly_wage_cents, triggers a notification, nor feeds any payroll export. Wage movement and tier promotion happen entirely off-system; the two workforce surfaces don't even reference each other's output.
evidence: supabase/migrations/641_workforce_performance_appraisals.sql and 705_j11 contain no pay_ladder/hourly_wage references; supabase/functions/performance-appraisals/index.ts only calls employee_appraisal_* RPCs

findings.title: Workforce gate data (certs, tooling, vendor logins) has no entry UI or API
findings.detail: Pay-ladder eligibility and service-scheduler suggestion badges depend on technician_oem_certifications, technician_in_house_certifications, technician_vendor_logins, and technician_profiles.tool_count — but workforce-api.ts exposes only fetch functions and WorkforceTechnicianPayLadderPage has zero mutations. This data can only be maintained via SQL or demo seeds, so both the ladder and scheduler quietly run on stale inputs.

findings.title: Duplicate outbound customer-comms pipelines; service messages invisible in QRM timeline
findings.detail: Service customer SMS/email flows through service_customer_notifications + service-customer-notify-dispatch (own Twilio/Resend wiring), while QRM has a parallel crm_communication_messages delivery stack (_shared/crm-communication-delivery.ts, also Twilio/Resend). Service comms never appear in the QRM customer communication history, and the delivery/retry/receipt logic is implemented twice.
evidence: supabase/functions/service-customer-notify-dispatch/index.ts:29-47; supabase/functions/_shared/crm-communication-delivery.ts (crm_communication_messages); no cross-writes between the two tables (grep supabase/functions for crm_communication_messages in service-*)

findings.title: RPO threshold dead-ends in a task instead of creating a deal
findings.detail: Roadmap L5.1 (mig 768) states 'RPO conversion creates a qrm_deals row carrying accrued credit', but the rental-rpo-threshold workflow only fires create_task. No code anywhere creates a qrm_deals/crm_deals row from rpo_credit_accrued_cents, so the sales pipeline never sees the conversion opportunity and the accrued credit must be re-keyed manually into a deal.
evidence: supabase/migrations/768_qep_stream_l_rental_department.sql:87; supabase/functions/_shared/flow-workflows/rental-lifecycle-flows.ts:216-235 (task only); grep for qrm_deals in rental code returns nothing

findings.title: Rental utilization KPI snapshots are written hourly but read by nothing
findings.detail: rental_snapshot_utilization writes 4 rental_* metrics to KPI snapshots every hour via pg_cron, yet no web surface queries those metric keys — RentalCommandCenterPage recomputes live via rental_compute_utilization RPC. The L6 'Command Center rental P&L lens' (rental AR exposure, idle carrying cost, RPO conversion rate, formula-visible drill from snapshots) was never built; the exec deck just links to /rentals.
evidence: supabase/migrations/774_l3_availability_reservations_utilization.sql:623-667; grep for rental_physical_utilization/rental_dollar_utilization in apps/web/src returns only database.types.ts; apps/web/src/features/exec/lib/department-view-deck.ts:46-53

findings.title: Fleet map is rental-blind and its controls are decorative
findings.detail: FleetMapPage never joins rental state: no on_rent/reserved/down-for-service coloring from qrm_equipment.readiness_status or rental_contract_lines (data the L0/L3 triggers maintain specifically for consumers), markers only red on 7d-stale telematics. The five overlay toggles mutate state nothing reads, and FilterBar filters are not connected to the query. The one map in the product cannot answer 'where is my rented iron'.
evidence: apps/web/src/features/fleet/pages/FleetMapPage.tsx:22-28,65-86 (overlays/markers ignore rental state); supabase/migrations/769_l0_rental_structural_refactor.sql:294-368 (fleet-state maintained for consumers)

findings.title: rental_availability_calendar has zero consumers
findings.detail: The deterministic per-unit/day calendar RPC (states on_rent/down_for_service/reserved/available over up to 92 days) is called nowhere in apps/web or any edge function — grep finds only its definition and database.types.ts. Counter reps have no availability grid; reservations are validated transactionally but never visualized, a workflow dead-end for the L3 slice's operator-facing half.
evidence: supabase/migrations/774_l3_availability_reservations_utilization.sql:292-345; grep for rental_availability_calendar across apps/web/src and supabase/functions returns no callers

findings.title: Two parallel equipment detail pages split capabilities and deep links
findings.detail: AssetDetailPage (/equipment/:id) has Commercial Action, tabs, countdowns, and KB matching but no edit; QrmEquipmentDetailPage (/qrm/equipment/:id) has edit/archive and EquipmentVision but none of the 360 tabs. Deep links diverge: 13 modules (service, fleet, rental command center, dashboards, inventory pressure) target /equipment/:id while SerialFirstWidget targets /qrm/equipment/:id, so which UX an operator gets depends on where they clicked. Both mount MachineLifecycleCard, duplicating fetches and layout.

findings.title: customer_fleet duplicates equipment identity; parts history only reachable two-hop
findings.detail: customer_fleet (082) re-declares make/model/year/serial_number/current_hours with a nullable equipment_id, creating a second machine registry that can drift from qrm_equipment (no sync trigger). parts_orders link to fleet_id, not equipment_id, so Asset 360's PartsTab must resolve customer_fleet first and shows nothing for machines without a fleet row — lifetime_parts_spend in badges and the parts list can disagree.

findings.title: machine_profiles (parts) and replacement_cost_curves duplicate a make/model reference concept with no link to equipment
findings.detail: The parts cluster's machine_profiles (261, populated by extract-machine-profiles from OEM PDFs with maintenance schedules and wear parts) is exactly the data equipment_service_intervals and replacement_cost_curves need, but there is no FK or join path to crm_equipment (make/model strings only, no consumer on the equipment side). Extracted maintenance schedules never become per-asset PM intervals.

findings.title: exec-summary-generator has zero callers; briefing logic triplicated
findings.detail: AiExecutiveSummaryStrip builds the identical briefing client-side ('so the surface stays reliable even if auxiliary briefing infrastructure is unavailable'), leaving the edge fn dead. evaluateBand + currency fmt helpers are copy-pasted across exec-summary-generator, exec-packet-generator, and AiExecutiveSummaryStrip — three drift points for threshold semantics.
evidence: supabase/functions/exec-summary-generator/index.ts (no invocations found outside its own dir); apps/web/src/features/exec/components/AiExecutiveSummaryStrip.tsx; supabase/functions/exec-packet-generator/index.ts (duplicate evaluateBand/fmt)

findings.title: /finance-enforcement is a navigation dead-end
findings.detail: The route is registered in App.tsx behind hasManagerOrAboveRole, but nav-config.ts and TopBar have no entry and no other module links to it. Worse, the CFO lens PolicyEnforcementWall routes finance exceptions to /exceptions and /service/invoice, never to the finance console that owns the enforcement tooling, and its page hardcodes workspaceId='default'.
evidence: apps/web/src/App.tsx:1117; grep of apps/web/src/lib/nav-config.ts for 'finance-enforcement' returns nothing; apps/web/src/features/exec/lib/policy-wall-actions.ts; apps/web/src/features/finance-enforcement/pages/FinanceEnforcementPage.tsx:27

findings.title: CFO command center never reads the finance foundation data
findings.detail: CfoCommandCenterView consumes only analytics snapshots; v_margin_matrix_summary, ar_dunning_events, vendor_invoices, form_8300_reports, and gl_periods never feed analytics_metric_definitions. The margin story is fractured across four disconnected sources: finance-enforcement MarginMatrixPanel (v_margin_matrix_summary), owner v_margin_exceptions (qb_margin_exceptions), exec MarginWaterfallExplorer (exec_margin_waterfall_v), and dashboards margin_analytics_view — no single reconciled margin number for leadership.

findings.title: Cluster surfaces are unreachable from app navigation
findings.detail: /decisions, /decisions/triage, /brief, and /email-drafts have route guards in App.tsx but no entry in NavRail.tsx or TopBar; /email-drafts is reachable only via one inline link in QRM Account360Tabs, /decisions and /brief only by typing the URL. Owner decision throughput (the module's whole point) depends on owners knowing a hidden URL.
evidence: apps/web/src/components/NavRail.tsx contains no references to decisions/email-drafts/brief/documents; only apps/web/src/features/qrm/components/Account360Tabs.tsx:1066 links to /email-drafts

findings.title: qep_decisions citations are dead text, not links into Document Center
findings.detail: Decision citations are freeform {source, ref, excerpt} JSON rendered as static cards in DecisionsPage; they carry no document_id or chunk_id even though the cited material lives in the same database's documents/chunks tables, and OmniCommand already supports /admin/documents/:id?chunk deep links. Owners approving decisions cannot verify evidence with one tap.
evidence: apps/web/src/features/decisions/lib/triage-api.ts:22-26 (TriageCitation shape), DecisionsPage.tsx CitationView vs apps/web/src/components/OmniCommand.tsx:213 deep-link format

findings.title: Two parallel knowledge-gap tables, only the legacy one has UI
findings.detail: document-router /ask writes low-confidence questions to document_knowledge_gaps (migration 342), but AdminPage's 'knowledge-gaps' tab reads and resolves only the older knowledge_gaps table from the chat KB. Gaps captured by Document Center Ask are never surfaced to the operators who curate content — duplicated entity, half-connected.

findings.title: Two unlinked decision systems: hub_decisions vs qep_decisions
findings.detail: The brief module's /brief/decisions log (hub_decisions, NotebookLM provenance, stakeholder-facing) and the owner decision queue (qep_decisions, lanes/gating/audit artifacts) never reference each other. A qep_decision resolved by the owner never appears in the stakeholder decision log, and hub_decisions rows have no code/lane linkage — the same real-world decision must be entered twice.
evidence: supabase/migrations/313_hub_decisions.sql (no qep_decision reference) vs 595_qep_decisions.sql; apps/web/src/features/brief/pages/BriefDecisionsPage.tsx reads hub_decisions only

findings.title: cross_department_alerts never reach their target departments
findings.detail: health-score-refresh generates alerts with a target_department column (service/parts/rentals/sales), but the only consumer is CrossDeptAlertFeed on the /nervous-system dashboard. No Floor widget, service/parts/rental page, or flow-engine trigger consumes them, so the 'every department sees signals from every other department' promise is one admin dashboard deep. Routing them through emit_event or a Floor attention signal would close the loop.
evidence: supabase/functions/health-score-refresh/index.ts:93 (generate_cross_department_alerts RPC); grep shows cross_department_alerts referenced only in apps/web/src/features/nervous-system/*

findings.title: auto-triage-pipeline has no caller — the decision inbox entry point is manual
findings.detail: The function is registered in supabase/config.toml and marked shipped in roadmap closeout migrations, but no UI, cron migration, or other edge function invokes it. features/decisions/lib/triage-api.ts reads qep_decisions directly. New pending decisions only become triage drafts if someone POSTs the endpoint by hand, so the precedent-matching pipeline sits idle.
evidence: grep of apps/web/src, supabase/functions, supabase/migrations finds no invocation; supabase/config.toml:818; apps/web/src/features/decisions/lib/triage-api.ts (direct table reads only); supabase/migrations/750_f14_auto_triage_pipeline_closeout.sql

findings.title: anomaly_alerts under-surfaced and stalled-deal logic triplicated
findings.detail: Only critical deal-scoped anomalies surface (qrm command-center useBlockers). activity_gap, embedding_stale, orphan_chunks, and non-critical pipeline_risk alerts have no operator surface at all. Meanwhile 'stalled deal' detection is independently re-implemented three times with different thresholds: anomaly-scan detectStallingDeals (7 days), floor StalledDealsTable/useFloorAttentionSignals (5/14 days), and the flow-engine context resolver — same signal, three sources of truth, none reconciled.

findings.title: Duplicate customer entities: customer_profiles_extended vs qrm_companies with no FK
findings.detail: Health scores, DGE customer DNA, and pricing personas live on customer_profiles_extended; the Floor, QRM, and portal operate on qrm_companies/crm_companies. CustomerHealthListWidget must count both tables separately for its coverage stat, and an at-risk profile row cannot deep-link to /qrm/companies/{id} because no foreign key or resolver connects the two entities. Every health/DNA surface outside nervous-system re-bridges by email or name matching.
evidence: apps/web/src/features/floor/widgets/CustomerHealthListWidget.tsx:47-71 (parallel counts, no join); apps/web/src/features/dge/lib/dge-api.ts:50-64 (lookup by email/hubspot/intellidealer id, not company id)

findings.title: ~20 deployed orphan functions inflate the attack/maintenance surface
findings.detail: Functions with zero frontend, cron, or internal callers: analytics-alert-evaluator, analytics-snapshot-runner, auto-triage-pipeline (calls lane-classifier but is itself uncalled), customer-dna-update, health-score-single, embed-qrm, qrm-reminder-dispatcher, crm-auth-audit, inbound-email-signal, kb-maintenance, iron-knowledge-ingest (scripts-only), document-onedrive-mirror, extract-machine-profiles, prospecting-tracker, requote-drafts, price-file-import (retired client lane), publish-price-sheet (partially), qb-rebate-deadlines-cron, qb-recommend-programs, marketing-engine, meta-social, deposit-calculator, exec-summary-generator is fine (called by exec-packet-generator) but the rest are dead ends. Each is a live authenticated HTTPS endpoint that must be kept secure.
evidence: Call map built from apps/web/src, supabase/migrations (functions/v1/* cron URLs), and cross-function greps; e.g. supabase/functions/auto-triage-pipeline/logic.ts, supabase/functions/inbound-email-signal/index.ts, supabase/functions/marketing-engine

findings.title: Decision OS pipeline half-wired: audit artifacts and voice-memo answers never fire
findings.detail: decision-audit-artifact (migrations 622, 763 closeout) and decision-voice-memo-answer (migration 754 closeout) are deployed with zero callers, while sibling functions decision-email-card/decision-linear-comment are driven by ratify-silence-runner. Decisions ratified through the email/Linear lanes never produce the tiered audit artifact the migrations were shipped for.

findings.title: L7 rental telematics/geofence has no live inbound provider path
findings.detail: L7 shipped geofence/telematics flow definitions (_shared/flow-workflows/rental-lifecycle-flows.ts, migration 778) but the only ways data enters are an internal-secret webhook nobody dispatches to and manual admin JWT entry (telematics-signal-ingest header). Adapters for Yanmar SmartAssist and generic providers exist in _shared/adapters but no scheduled poller or provider-facing dispatcher function is deployed, so predictive fleet intelligence runs on hand-entered data.

findings.title: Duplicated service billing/notification logic left as dead twins
findings.detail: service-invoice-generator and service-notifications have zero callers; their responsibilities are handled by service-billing-post (frontend-invoked) and service-customer-notify-dispatch (cron, migration 105) respectively. service-haul-router likewise has no frontend or cron caller (only shares _shared/service-lifecycle-notify.ts). Divergent invoice logic risks drift if anyone revives the dead twin instead of the live path.

findings.title: Event fabric is blind to parts and service
findings.detail: emit_event() DB triggers exist only for voice (360), hub feedback (321), and rental (775/776/778). Parts and service keep module-local logs (parts_order_events, service_job_events, quote_availability_events) that never reach flow_events, so Flow Engine workflows cannot react to a backordered part, a blocked service job, or a completed inspection the way they now react to rental lifecycle events.
evidence: grep emit_event over supabase/migrations returns only 194,196,321,360,361,768,775,776,778; parts_order_events/service_job_events created without emitters

findings.title: Equipment identity fragmented across five entities
findings.detail: qrm_equipment (canonical dealer units), machine_profiles (245 — parts' model reference, no FK to anything equipment-side), qb_equipment_models (286 — quote builder's private catalog), customer_fleet (082 — duplicates make/model/year/serial columns with an optional FK to crm_equipment), and equipment_base_codes. Model/spec data is re-entered per module; a Yanmar model exists as four unlinked rows.

findings.title: Six quote entities, no unified quote spine
findings.detail: quotes (029, legacy CRM), quote_packages (087, anchored to crm_deals with own quote_signatures), qb_quotes (286, the active builder), parts_quotes, service_quotes, and portal_quote_reviews each carry separate line-item, signature, and audit tables. qb_quotes has no FK to quotes or quote_packages; legacy quotes still has 6 edge-function call sites. Cross-department quoting (machine + parts + service on one deal) requires manual re-entry.

findings.title: Imported IntelliDealer AR aging is a dead-end table
findings.detail: qrm_ar_open_items (434) holds the dealership's actual AR aging from IntelliDealer imports but has zero edge-function consumers and appears in the frontend only via database.types.ts. Rental's credit gate (770) and account-360 use ar_credit_blocks instead, and the dunning cycle (664) works off customer_invoices — so real imported receivables never inform credit holds or dunning.
evidence: supabase/migrations/434_qrm_ar_open_items.sql; grep qrm_ar_open_items under supabase/functions returns nothing; 770_l0_rental_checkout_security_gate.sql uses ar_credit_blocks

findings.title: Advisors add part requirements blind: no availability shown at requirement entry, so backorder risk is discovered only after running the planner
findings.detail: PartsRequirementEditor (the service UI for adding requirement lines) performs no lookup against parts_catalog, parts_inventory, or the m673 lookup engine — grep for parts_catalog/parts_inventory/on_hand/match_parts in the component returns nothing — and service-parts-manager's add action (index.ts:195-230) accepts any part_number string without validating it exists or has stock. The advisor learns whether a part is on the shelf or weeks out only after invoking service-parts-planner, which then sets the promise path. Meanwhile the counter has a hybrid AI lookup (ai-parts-lookup returning stock_on_hand) that the service surface never calls.
evidence: supabase/functions/ai-parts-lookup/index.ts:104,180 (stock_on_hand exists in counter lookup, unused by service)
findings.recommendation: Wire PartsRequirementEditor to the same lookup used by the companion (ai-parts-lookup / match_parts_hybrid) to show per-branch on-hand, price, and lead-time hints inline as the advisor types, and warn immediately when the requirement will force a vendor order past the job's promised date.

findings.title: Owner cockpit stacks a 90s page poll, realtime invalidation, and five widget-level pollers
findings.detail: OwnerDashboardPage refetches owner_dashboard_summary every 90s AND wires useDashboardRealtime to invalidate the same key on live events -- the poll is largely redundant with realtime. Owner widgets each add their own intervals (OwnershipHealthDial 120s, TeamSignalsGrid 180s, BranchStackHeatmap 180s, OwnerBriefCard 300s, MarginExceptionsPage 120s, DataMinerEquivalentsPage 120s), so an open owner screen sustains 6-7 independent polling loops. Repo-wide there are 76 refetchInterval sites, so background query volume compounds across dashboards.
findings.recommendation: Where realtime invalidation exists, lengthen or drop the interval poll; standardize widget polling through a shared config (e.g. one 3-5 min interval constant) and pause polling when the tab is hidden via refetchIntervalInBackground defaults.

findings.title: Parts import conflicts page polls the run every 10 seconds forever and refetches all conflicts unbounded
findings.detail: ImportConflictsPage polls fetchImportRun (.select('*') .single()) on refetchInterval: 10000 with no stop condition -- it keeps hammering every 10s even after the run reaches a terminal state. fetchRunConflicts does parts_import_conflicts .select('*') for the run with no .limit(), so a large import (thousands of conflicted rows) lands fully in the browser and is filtered client-side.
findings.recommendation: Make refetchInterval a function that returns false once run.status is terminal, and paginate conflicts server-side (or at least .limit() + fetch-next-on-resolve, which fits the existing one-at-a-time cursor UX).

findings.title: App.tsx is a 2,999-line single-file route registry with only ~16KB of headroom left under the entry cap
findings.detail: Code-splitting is done correctly — 192 React.lazy declarations, no eager feature imports — but all route declarations, guard wrappers, and redirect logic live in one 2,999-line App.tsx that is fully parsed in the entry bundle. The built index entry is 183,199 B against a 199,711 B cap (baseline 181,555 B), leaving ~16.5KB before CI fails; every new route, guard branch, or role-permission import (the canAccess* family from nav-config/home-route) lands in this file and eats the budget. PortalRoutes.tsx already shows the scalable pattern: a feature-local route-element module whose page imports are lazy, keeping only Route wiring in the entry.
findings.recommendation: Extract per-domain route groups (service, parts, qrm, admin, rental) into feature-local *Routes.tsx modules following the PortalRoutes pattern. This flattens entry growth per new route to near zero and stops the recurring collision with the index-entry byte cap.

findings.title: RLS initplan check passes ('scanned 413 post-baseline migrations') but has a bare-spelling blind spot
findings.detail: Ran `node scripts/check-rls-initplan.mjs`: output was 'rls initplan check passed: scanned 413 post-baseline migrations'. The per-row re-evaluation risk in live policies is genuinely mitigated — migration 365 rewrote the entire live policy catalog to (select helper()) form, and an independent regex sweep of all CREATE POLICY statements found 0 unwrapped calls in migrations >= 366 (the 1,017 unwrapped statements in 186 pre-365 files are superseded at runtime by 365's catalog rewrite, though they re-apply briefly on any fresh db reset until 365 runs). Residual gap: the script's RAW_PATTERNS only match the `public.`-prefixed spellings plus bare auth.uid()/auth.role() (scripts/check-rls-initplan.mjs:8-14), so a future policy written as bare `get_my_role()` or using `auth.jwt()` per-row would pass the gate undetected; it also skips policies created via dynamic SQL (execute format(...)).
findings.recommendation: Extend RAW_PATTERNS with schema-unqualified spellings (get_my_role(), get_my_workspace(), get_my_audience()) and auth.jwt(), and add a second pass that flags CREATE POLICY built through execute format(...) for manual review.

findings.title: crm-router auth path constructs 3-4 Supabase clients per request and discards one immediately
findings.detail: Every crm-router/qrm-router request builds a fresh admin client plus a caller client in createRequestContext (crm-router-service.ts:49-56), then hydrateCaller discards that caller client and builds a second one (line 78); resolveCallerContext internally builds a third caller client (dge-auth.ts:262) and resolveServiceWorkspaceId can build a fourth (dge-auth.ts:176). Beyond client construction overhead, the auth path adds a GoTrue /auth/v1/user HTTP round trip (dge-auth.ts:208) plus, when claims are missing, a sequential profiles read (line 286-291) and get_my_workspace RPC (line 297) — those two are also serially awaited though independent. The admin client is never request-specific and could live at module scope (demo-admin already does this at demo-admin/index.ts:17).
findings.recommendation: Hoist the admin client to module scope, create exactly one caller client per request and thread it through createRequestContext → hydrateCaller → resolveCallerContext, and parallelize the profile read and get_my_workspace RPC fallback with Promise.all.

findings.title: Rental contract lifecycle transition fans out to per-line hold updates, each re-firing a per-row qrm_equipment fleet-state recompute
findings.detail: One lifecycle_state UPDATE on rental_contracts runs through 3 BEFORE triggers (770 gate, 772 stamping, 776 close-billing gate which itself queries rental_invoices) and then AFTER triggers: rental_maintain_reservation_holds (774:165) updates every active hold on the contract, and each hold row fires trg_rental_holds_fleet_state (774:419) which calls rental_recompute_equipment_fleet_state — a SELECT plus an UPDATE on qrm_equipment per hold. A 10-line contract going on_rent therefore executes ~10 hold updates + 10 equipment recomputes + the 775 event emit + pg_notify, all in the operator's transaction. Bounded by the IS NOT DISTINCT FROM guard (774:110) so it only fires on real transitions, but multi-line contracts pay linear trigger cost at checkout/return — the operator-facing hot path.
findings.recommendation: Make trg_rental_holds_fleet_state a statement-level trigger with a transition table (or debounce recompute per distinct equipment_id within the transaction) so an N-line transition recomputes each unit once instead of once per hold row.

findings.title: Sub-hourly cron density: an every-minute job, an every-2-minute job, and five */5 jobs run around the clock regardless of activity
findings.detail: hub-feedback-notify-every-min (322) fires a pg_net http_post to an edge function every minute — 1,440 invocations/day for an internal feedback notifier (the query itself is indexed via idx_hub_feedback_events_unsent and batched at 50, so cadence is the only issue). hub-feedback-preview-poll runs every 2 minutes (327). clean-rate-limits, pipeline-enforcer-periodic, service-tat-monitor, service-stage-enforcer, and qrm-recommend-moves-periodic all run */5; m365 token refresh and mailbox sync both run */10; qb-price-sheet-watchdog, hub-changelog, embed-crm-refresh, and service-vendor-escalator run */15. On top of that, rental-utilization-snapshot-hourly recomputes a trailing-365-day rental_invoices aggregate and 30-day line-day scans per workspace every hour (774:557-561) for metrics whose inputs change at most daily. Aggregate: 20+ scheduled scans per hour at steady state on a single Supabase instance.
findings.recommendation: Tier the schedules: event-driven paths (hub feedback already writes events; emit_event fires pg_notify) can replace minute-level polling; relax hub-feedback-notify to */5 and preview-poll to */10; move the 365-day dollar-utilization aggregate out of the hourly snapshot into the existing daily rental-intelligence job.

findings.title: Exec and floor surfaces deep-link to the builder generically instead of the specific quotes
findings.detail: exec metric-actions maps quote_expiring_7d to a bare buildQuoteBuilderHref() ('Open quote builder') with no expiring-quote filter or package id, so a manager investigating the KPI lands on a blank new-quote wizard; the quote list supports status/search params (buildQuoteListUrl) that these callers ignore.

findings.title: Voice origination channel and two promised events have no writers
findings.detail: origination_channel='voice' is a legal CHECK value (mig 769) and L6.1 lists a 'Voice-to-rental extraction target', but voice-extract-entities/voice-to-qrm contain no rental path — only counter, iron, and portal channels have writers. Similarly the L4 roadmap promises rental.availability.low and rental.cycle.due events plus a rental-availability-low workflow; neither event is emitted by rental_lifecycle_scan nor listed in the flow-synthesize catalog.

findings.title: EaaS tables are schema-only and FleetMap overlays/filters are cosmetic
findings.detail: eaas_subscriptions/eaas_usage_records (084) have zero frontend consumers — the Equipment-as-a-Service moonshot never got a surface. On FleetMapPage the FilterBar (branch/make/customer) and five overlay toggles (idle assets, service routes, customer concentration) are rendered but not connected to any query or map layer, so the page is markers-only.
evidence: supabase/migrations/084_equipment_as_a_service.sql; grep for eaas_ in apps/web/src returns nothing; apps/web/src/features/fleet/pages/FleetMapPage.tsx:16-28,100-107

findings.title: Owner cockpit Service Backlog tile is a hardcoded stub
findings.detail: The Tier-3 KPI tile renders hero '—' with subline 'Wire-up lands in Slice F with service_dashboard_rollup' while working service labor data already exists one page away in owner_data_miner_service_labor — data exists but is not surfaced on the primary owner surface.

findings.title: Exec packet 'emailed' delivery status has no email dispatch
findings.detail: CommandCenterExportMenu lets a user mark a packet 'emailed' (updating exec_packet_runs.delivery_status/delivered_at) but nothing actually sends it — no wiring to draft-email/SendGrid infrastructure that exists elsewhere in supabase/functions. The board packet loop ends at manual markdown download, inviting a false audit trail.

findings.title: Document fact verification is displayed but impossible to perform
findings.detail: document_facts carries verified_by/verified_at and ContextPaneFacts renders a 'verified' badge, but document-router's handler exposes no fact-verify endpoint and the frontend adapter has no mutation — so no human can ever mark a fact verified, and the obligations graph is built entirely on unverified extractions.
evidence: apps/web/src/routes/admin/documents/ContextPaneFacts.tsx:72-85; supabase/functions/document-router/handler.ts has no /fact* route; features/documents/router.ts has no verify function

findings.title: The Floor has no rental role or rental widgets despite Stream L shipping
findings.detail: FLOOR_WIDGET_REGISTRY contains zero rental.* widgets and the IronRole set has no rental coordinator; the only rental data on The Floor is BuPulseStrip's single owner tile reading rental_contracts. Stream L shipped a rental command center, reservations, returns, billing, and predictive fleet intelligence (migs 768-778), but the operator home surface never surfaces off-rent alerts, upcoming returns, or utilization to any role.
evidence: apps/web/src/features/floor/lib/floor-widget-registry.tsx (no rental.* ids; ALL_ROLES has 7 roles, none rental); apps/web/src/features/floor/widgets/BuPulseStrip.tsx:164 (single rental_contracts read); supabase/migrations/774-778 (Stream L rental schema)

findings.title: Tier-4 QRM rename cutover stalled at aliases
findings.detail: qrm-router is live and the frontend uses it, but the parallel aliases embed-qrm and qrm-reminder-dispatcher have zero callers anywhere: the embedding cron (migration 332) still targets embed-crm and hubspot-webhook still forwards into crm-router. The stated plan in qrm-router/index.ts ('a future cutover migration will remove crm-router') has no follow-through, leaving duplicate deployed endpoints per function.

findings.title: Rental predictive layer forks parts forecasting instead of sharing it
findings.detail: 778 creates rental_demand_forecasts as an admitted 'parts_demand_forecasts clone, category-keyed' with its own cron and drivers format, rather than generalizing a shared demand-forecast substrate. Combined with the 768 discovery note that all rental tables had zero production rows, the newly wired rental intelligence runs on demo-seeded data only.
evidence: supabase/migrations/778_l7_predictive_fleet_intelligence.sql header ('parts_demand_forecasts clone'); supabase/migrations/768_qep_stream_l_rental_department.sql ('production rows: ZERO across all of them')
